definition_zh: 胡说；废话；荒唐的事；荒唐行为；无意义的文字
definition_en: words or ideas that have no meaning or logic; foolish behaviour or a silly plan; something absurd or worthless; also a style of writing that plays with meaningless language
core_image: 一张纸上写满歪歪扭扭的字，读出声却一句也讲不通
scene: 桌上那张纸写满了字，读出声却发现前后毫不相干。 The report was full of nonsense and changed nothing.
sceneCN: 这里 nonsense 是「胡说、废话」（第 1 个义项：没有意义或逻辑的话语）；句意是那份报告满篇胡言，什么也没有改变。图中可辨识物件：写满字的纸、桌面。

pos.zh: 胡说；废话；荒唐的事；荒唐行为

derivatives.zh: 由 nonsense 加形容词后缀 -ical 构成，义为「荒谬的；讲不通的」
由 nonsensical 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「荒谬地」
由 no 与 nonsense 复合而成，义为「务实的；不讲情面的」

senses.title: Words that make no sense
senses.definition: spoken or written words that have no meaning or logic
senses.definitionCN: 说出的或写下的话语没有任何意义或逻辑
senses.example: What he said was nonsense from beginning to end.
senses.exampleCN: 他从头到尾说的都是废话。
senses.why: The word joins a negative prefix to the noun for meaning, so its first job is to mark language that carries no sense at all.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把否定前缀接到表示意义的名词上，所以它最初的本职就是标记完全不带意义的语言。

senses.title: Foolish behaviour or a silly plan
senses.definition: behaviour or a plan that is silly and should not be taken seriously
senses.definitionCN: 愚蠢且不值得当真的行为或计划
senses.example: The idea of painting the roof at midnight was pure nonsense.
senses.exampleCN: 半夜去刷屋顶这个主意纯属胡闹。
senses.why: Once words are judged empty, the same judgement passes to actions, because a plan that makes no sense is exactly what the word already rejects.
senses.whyCN: 一旦话被判定为空，同一把尺子就量到行动上，因为讲不通的计划正是这个词本来要否定的东西。

senses.title: Something absurd or worthless
senses.titleCN: 荒唐的事；毫无价值的东西
senses.definition: a thing or situation so absurd that it seems unworthy of serious attention
senses.definitionCN: 荒唐到似乎不值得认真对待的事物或局面
senses.example: The whole ceremony struck the villagers as nonsense.
senses.exampleCN: 整场仪式在村民看来荒唐得很。
senses.why: The noun can point at the thing rather than at the talk, so anything that looks pointless can be labelled with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词可以不指话语而指事情本身，于是任何看起来没有意义的东西都能用同一个词来贴标签。

senses.title: A literary style built on meaningless words
senses.definition: a kind of writing, especially verse, that uses invented or meaningless words for comic or musical effect
senses.definitionCN: 一种使用生造词或无意义词以取得诙谐或音乐效果的文体，尤指诗歌
senses.example: The children loved the nonsense verse more than the serious poems.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们喜欢那些荒诞诗胜过严肃的诗。
senses.why: Nonsense can be made on purpose, and writers turned the defect into a genre, keeping the word while changing its purpose from blame to delight.
senses.whyCN: 无意义的东西也可以被故意造出来，作家把这个缺陷变成一种文体，词没有变，用途却从责备转成了取乐。

intro.en: Nonsense is a Latin prefix and a Latin noun joined in English, so it says on its surface exactly what it means.
intro.cn: nonsense 是一个拉丁前缀和一个拉丁名词在英语里拼合而成，字面上就把它自己的意思说了出来。

items.en: The negative particle non meant not, and Latin already used it to deny the word that followed.
items.cn: 否定小词 non 意为「不」，拉丁语中已用它来否定后面的词。

items.en: Sensus meant feeling, perception or meaning, and it came from the verb sentire, to feel.
items.cn: sensus 意为感觉、感知或意义，出自动词 sentire（感觉）。

items.en: English fixed the borrowed prefix to the borrowed noun, and the new word plainly announced no sense.
items.cn: 英语把借来的前缀固定在借来的名词上，新词直白地宣告「没有意义」。

items.en: Dictionaries generally date the noun to the early seventeenth century, when it first named foolish talk.
items.cn: 一般认为这个名词起于十七世纪初，最初指愚蠢的言谈。

items.en: Modern English extends it to foolish behaviour, absurd things and a playful literary style.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到荒唐行为、荒谬事物以及一种戏谑的文体。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem for feeling and meaning; the near-meaning group collects other labels for empty or absurd talk.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「感觉、意义」词干上的词；近义组收其他给空洞或荒唐话语贴标签的词。

entries.definition: The meaning a word carries, or a faculty that perceives.
entries.definitionCN: 词语携带的意义，或感知的能力。

entries.definition: Without meaning, or without consciousness.
entries.definitionCN: 没有意义的，或失去知觉的。

entries.definition: A feeling in the body, or a burst of public excitement.
entries.definitionCN: 身体上的感觉，或公众的一阵激动。

entries.definition: Connected with the senses of the body.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体感官有关的。

entries.definition: Worthless material, or talk that deserves no attention.
entries.definitionCN: 没有价值的东西，或根本不值得理会的话。

entries.definition: The quality of being wildly unreasonable.
entries.definitionCN: 极端不合情理的性质。

entries.definition: Foolish behaviour or a foolish undertaking.
entries.definitionCN: 愚蠢的行为或荒唐的举动。

entries.definition: Speech that is impossible to understand.
entries.definitionCN: 无法听懂的话。

normalIntro.en: The word is non plus sense, and the joint is so plain that English keeps making new words with the same prefix.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 non 加 sense，接合处太直白，所以英语一直用同一前缀造新词。

normal.en: The word is non plus sense, a negative prefix fixed to the noun for meaning.
normal.cn: 这个词是 non 加 sense：一个否定前缀接在表示意义的名词上。

normal.en: Sensus in Latin meant perception as well as meaning, so the word denies sensible feeling along with sense.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 sensus 既指感知也指意义，所以这个词否定的既是意义，也是合乎情理的感觉。

normal.en: The prefix non- stays productive in English, which is why forms such as nonissue appear so easily.
normal.cn: 前缀 non- 在英语里一直能产，所以像 nonissue 这样的形式很容易冒出来。

normal.en: Nonsense verse is a real genre, so the word can name a deliberate art and not only a mistake.
normal.cn: nonsense verse 是一种真实存在的文体，可见这个词既指错误，也能指刻意的艺术。

normal.en: No-nonsense as an adjective means practical and unwilling to waste time, a reversal of the noun's reputation.
normal.cn: no-nonsense 作形容词指务实、不肯浪费时间，正好把这名词的名声翻了个面。

abstract.en: A word that says no sense needs no metaphor, because its two parts already perform the judgement.
abstract.cn: 一个说「没有意义」的词不需要比喻，它的两个构件本身就已经做出了判断。

abstract.en: The same label serves for empty talk, foolish acts and a comic art, since all three begin by refusing meaning.
abstract.cn: 同一个标签能用于空话、蠢事和一种诙谐艺术，因为三者都从拒绝意义开始。

abstract.en: Its playful fourth sense shows that a defect can be cultivated until it becomes a style.
abstract.cn: 它那个戏谑的第四义说明：缺陷也能被培养，直到长成一种风格。

examples.en: What he said was nonsense from beginning to end.
examples.cn: 他从头到尾说的都是废话。

examples.en: The report was full of nonsense and changed nothing.
examples.cn: 那份报告满篇胡言，什么也没改变。

examples.en: The children loved the nonsense verse more than the serious poems.
examples.cn: 孩子们喜欢那些荒诞诗胜过严肃的诗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弄三思」——弄来弄去、三思再想也讲不通，那就是废话；记住 nonsense 是胡说。

root: non-（拉丁语否定前缀「不」）加 sense（拉丁语 sensus「感觉、意义」）构成，一般认为十七世纪初进入英语，最初指愚蠢的言谈。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is language without meaning; the senses widen to foolish acts, absurd things and a literary style that makes meaninglessness on purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是没有意义的语言；义项由此扩展到愚蠢行为、荒谬事物，以及故意制造无意义的文体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet covered in crooked writing that falls apart the moment it is read aloud.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张写满歪扭字迹的纸，一读出声就散成一片。

branches.en: a speech that loses its thread after one sentence
branches.cn: 说了一句话就断了线的发言

branches.en: a crowd shaking its head at an empty promise
branches.cn: 众人对着空头承诺摇头

branches.en: a ladder raised at midnight to paint a roof
branches.cn: 半夜架起梯子去刷屋顶

branches.en: a ceremony that no villager can take seriously
branches.cn: 村民没人当真的一场仪式

branches.en: children chanting invented words in a ring
branches.cn: 孩子们围成一圈念生造词

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin negative prefix and the Latin noun for feeling and meaning, with English suffixes extending the family.
intro.cn: 这个词立在拉丁语否定前缀与表示感觉、意义的名词上，英语词尾又把词族往外延伸。

latinIntro.en: Latin non supplies the negation and Latin sensus, from sentire, supplies the noun of meaning; English did the joining.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 non 提供否定，拉丁语 sensus（出自 sentire）提供表示意义的名词；拼合则是英语完成的。

definition_zh: 延伸；扩建部分；延期；电话分机
definition_en: the act of making something longer or larger; an added part of a building; extra time; a phone line connected to one system
core_image: 原本的房屋旁边又接出一间，电话线也分出一条
scene: 我们申请延长截止日期。 We asked for an extension of the deadline.
sceneCN: 这里 extension 是「延期」（第 3 个义项）；句意：我们申请延长截止日期。

derivatives.zh: 延伸；延长

senses.title: The act of extending
senses.definition: the act of making something longer or larger
senses.definitionCN: 使某物更长或更大的行为
senses.example: The extension of the railway took two years.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路的延伸用了两年。
senses.why: The core sense is the act of stretching out.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是向外伸展的行为。

senses.title: An added part
senses.definition: an extra part added to a building
senses.definitionCN: 加建在建筑物上的额外部分
senses.example: They built a small extension at the back.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在后面建了一个小扩建部分。
senses.why: The act becomes the added structure.
senses.whyCN: 动作变成加建的结构。

senses.title: Extra time
senses.definition: extra time allowed to finish something
senses.definitionCN: 为完成某事而允许的额外时间
senses.example: The teacher gave us an extension.
senses.exampleCN: 老师给了我们延期。
senses.why: Stretching in space becomes stretching in time.
senses.whyCN: 空间上的延伸变成时间上的延长。

senses.title: Phone line
senses.definition: a phone line connected to a main line
senses.definitionCN: 连接到主线上的电话分线
senses.example: Call me on extension twenty two.
senses.exampleCN: 请拨分机二十二找我。
senses.why: A branch line extends from the main one.
senses.whyCN: 分线从主线上延伸出来。

intro.en: Extension comes from Latin extensio, from extendere, to stretch out.
intro.cn: extension 来自拉丁语 extensio，根源是 extendere（向外拉伸）。

items.en: Extendere means to stretch out.
items.cn: extendere 意为向外拉伸。

items.en: Extensio means a stretching out.
items.cn: extensio 意为向外伸展。

items.en: Extension keeps the sense of enlargement.
items.cn: 古法语中 extension 保留「扩大」之义。

items.en: Extension names an added part or extra time.
items.cn: extension 指加建部分或额外时间。

items.en: Extension also means a phone branch line.
items.cn: 现代英语中 extension 也指电话分机。

entries.definition: the state of being stretched tight

entries.definition: the act of watching or listening carefully

entries.definition: something added to a building

entries.definition: the act of making something last longer
entries.definitionCN: 延长

entries.definition: an extra building added to a main one

normalIntro.en: Extension is the noun of extend, covering added space, added time, and added phone lines.
normalIntro.cn: extension 是 extend 的名词，涵盖加建空间、延长时间与电话分线。

normal.en: The library needs an extension at the back.
normal.cn: 图书馆需要在后面加建一部分。

normal.en: She asked for an extension on the essay.
normal.cn: 她申请延长交论文的期限。

normal.en: Please dial extension thirty five.
normal.cn: 请拨分机三十五。

normal.en: The extension of the road eased traffic.
normal.cn: 道路的延伸缓解了交通。

normal.en: He plugged the lamp into an extension lead.
normal.cn: 他把台灯插到延长线插座上。

abstract.en: Picture a small room added to the side of a house.
abstract.cn: 想象房子侧面加出一个小房间。

abstract.en: Imagine a clock whose hands move more slowly.
abstract.cn: 想象一只指针走得更慢的钟。

abstract.en: Think of one main road splitting into a side lane.
abstract.cn: 想象一条主路分出一条侧道。

examples.en: The council approved the extension of the school.
examples.cn: 议会批准了学校的扩建。

examples.en: He was given a two week extension.
examples.cn: 他获得了两周的延期。

examples.en: Her office extension is not working.
examples.cn: 她办公室的分机坏了。

sensesIntro.en: Extension means the act of extending, an added building, extra time, or a phone branch line.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a new room attached to an old house.
core.cn: 核心意象：老房子旁新接出的一间房。

branches.en: The base sense is the act of stretching out.
branches.cn: 基础义是向外伸展的行为。

branches.en: The act becomes an added structure.
branches.cn: 动作变成加建的结构。

branches.en: Stretching in space becomes extra time.
branches.cn: 空间延伸变成额外时间。

branches.en: A branch line extends from the main line.
branches.cn: 分线从主线上延伸出来。

branches.en: The act of extending and its built result are linked.
branches.cn: 延伸行为与其建成的结果相互关联。

intro.en: Extension is extend plus -sion, a noun ending seen in expansion and tension.
intro.cn: extension 由 extend 加 -sion 构成，-sion 是见于 expansion、tension 的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin extensio and extendere are the source forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 extensio 与 extendere 是来源形式。

definition_zh: 尖端；小费；顶端；倾倒；给小费
definition_en: the pointed end of something, extra money for service, or to tilt and empty a container
core_image: 一根手指能点住的顶端；桌面一角翘起的倾斜
scene: 笔尖在纸上洇出一小团墨。 Ink spread from the tip of his pen.
sceneCN: 这里 tip 是「尖端」（第 1 个义项：物体最细最前的末端）；句意：墨水从他笔尖洇开。

collocations.zh: 使天平倾斜；起决定作用

derivatives.zh: tip 加 -sy，义为「微醉的；站不稳的」（由倾斜义引申）
tip 加 -ster，义为「提供内幕消息者；赛马预测者」
tip + point 复合，义为「临界点；引爆点」

senses.title: The pointed or far end
senses.definition: the thin, pointed or extreme end of something long or sharp
senses.definitionCN: 细长或锐利物体的最末端
senses.example: The pencil broke at the tip.
senses.exampleCN: 铅笔在笔尖处断了。
senses.why: The core image is a point you can touch with one finger.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一根手指就能点住的顶点。

senses.title: A small sum for service
senses.definition: extra money given to someone for a service, beyond the price
senses.definitionCN: 服务价格之外另给的酬金
senses.example: He left a tip for the waiter.
senses.exampleCN: 他给服务员留了小费。
senses.why: Money handed over at the end, like the end of a transaction.
senses.whyCN: 交易末尾递出的钱，如事物之「末端」。

senses.title: A useful hint
senses.definition: a small piece of practical advice or advance information
senses.definitionCN: 一小条实用建议或内幕消息
senses.example: She gave me a tip about the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 她给了我一则关于考试的小提示。
senses.why: A small item that tilts your understanding or plans.
senses.whyCN: 一条小消息让局面为你倾斜。

senses.title: To tilt or overturn
senses.definition: to lean to one side, or to make something fall by tilting it
senses.definitionCN: 侧向一边，或使某物倾覆
senses.example: The boat tipped in the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 小船在风中倾斜。
senses.why: The end swings down as the whole leans.
senses.whyCN: 整体倾斜时，末端先落。

senses.title: To empty by tilting
senses.definition: to pour out the contents of a container by tilting it
senses.definitionCN: 倾斜容器把里面的东西倒出来
senses.example: He tipped the box of nails onto the bench.
senses.exampleCN: 他把一盒钉子倒在长凳上。
senses.why: Tilting leads directly to emptying.
senses.whyCN: 倾斜自然导向倒空。

senses.title: To give a tip of money
senses.definition: to give extra money to a person for a service
senses.definitionCN: 为服务支付额外的钱
senses.example: Passengers tipped the porter a pound.
senses.exampleCN: 乘客给了搬运工一镑小费。
senses.why: The noun of money becomes the act of giving it.
senses.whyCN: 钱的名词变成给钱的行为。

senses.title: The top of a structure or region
senses.definition: the highest or furthest point of something, such as a mountain
senses.definitionCN: 某物最高或最远之点，如山顶
senses.example: Snow covered the tip of the mountain.
senses.exampleCN: 山顶覆盖着雪。
senses.why: The farthest end upward is still an end.
senses.whyCN: 向上的最远端仍是末端。

senses.title: To tip off: warn in advance
senses.definition: to warn someone privately before something happens
senses.definitionCN: 事前私下提醒或告发
senses.example: Someone tipped off the police about the raid.
senses.exampleCN: 有人向警方事先透露了突袭计划。
senses.why: Information tilts the outcome before the event lands.
senses.whyCN: 消息让结局在事件落地前先行倾斜。

intro.en: Tip is a Germanic word of double origin: one line from Old Norse or Low German meaning the point or end, another from later usage meaning to tap or strike, which led to tilting and to the slang of small payment.
intro.cn: tip 在日耳曼语中有双线来源：一线出自古诺斯语或低地德语，意为尖端；另一线为后期用法「轻敲、击打」，引申出倾斜与小费的俚语义。

items.en: Tip meant the point or top of a thing.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 tip 指物体的尖端或顶部。

items.en: Tip named ends of blades, fingers and poles.
items.cn: 中古英语 tip 用来指刀刃、指尖与杆的末端。

items.en: The verb grew: to tip meant to tap, then to tilt and overturn.
items.cn: 十六世纪动词扩展：由轻敲而倾斜、翻倒。

items.en: Tipping grew into handing over, and slang made a tip a small gift of money.
items.cn: 十七世纪 tipping 衍生为递出，俚语中 tip 成为小额赏钱。

items.en: A tip as a hint spread from racing slang into everyday advice.
items.cn: 十九世纪 tip 表内幕消息，由赛马俚语进入日常建议。

items.en: Modern usage keeps ends, tilts, fees and hints side by side.
items.cn: 现代用法并置尖端、倾斜、小费与提示。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alike short -ip words; the second sorts end-and-hint neighbours.
note.cn: 第一组是 -ip 结尾的形近短词；第二组列出末端与提示义的近邻。

entries.definitionCN: 浸；蘸

entries.definitionCN: 山峰；最高点

definition_zh: 好斗的；侵略的；积极进取的；强势的；侵袭性的；强效的；激进的
definition_en: ready to attack or quarrel, forceful and determined in pursuing a goal, or strong and severe in its effects
core_image: 向前迈出一步，把身体逼到别人面前的那股劲
scene: 销售例会上，新来的主管把下季度目标写满整面白板，逐条压到每个小组头上。 The firm launched an aggressive campaign to win younger customers.
sceneCN: 这里 aggressive 是「强势的、猛烈的」（第 4 个义项：营销与推销上的强硬做法）；句意为这家公司发起了一场猛烈的推广活动，以争取更年轻的顾客。白板上写满目标，会议室里气氛紧绷。

pos.zh: 形容词：好斗的、有攻击性的；侵略的；积极进取的；强势的

collocations.zh: 好斗的行为；攻击性行为
强势营销；猛烈的市场推广

derivatives.zh: 与本源出拉丁语名词 aggressio，义为「侵略；攻击行为；（心理上的）攻击性」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「咄咄逼人地；强势地」
由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「好斗；攻击性；闯劲」
与本源出拉丁语动词 aggredi，义为「侵略者；挑衅者」

senses.title: Hostile and ready to attack
senses.definition: of a person or animal, angry and ready to attack or quarrel
senses.definitionCN: 指人或动物怒气冲冲、随时准备动手或争吵
senses.example: The dog became aggressive whenever a stranger came near the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 只要有陌生人靠近大门，那条狗就变得凶猛。
senses.why: Latin aggredi is ad- 'towards' plus gradi 'to step'; the word pictures a step taken at someone in order to strike.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 aggredi 由 ad-「朝向」加 gradi「走、迈步」构成，词里画的是朝对方迈步逼近、准备动手的姿态，所以最先长出的是「好斗」这一具体义。

senses.title: Invading by force
senses.definition: of a country, an army or an action, using force to take over another place or to dominate others
senses.definitionCN: 指国家、军队或行动以武力侵占他处或压制他人
senses.example: The smaller nation condemned the aggressive moves along its border.
senses.exampleCN: 那个小国谴责邻国在其边境的侵略举动。
senses.why: Scale the same forward step up to an army: stepping into someone else's land is exactly what aggression looks like between states.
senses.whyCN: 把同一个「向前迈步」放大到军队身上：踏进别人的土地，正是国家之间所说的侵略，所以这一义项保留的仍是迈步逼近的动作，只是主体换成了军队。

senses.title: Forceful in pursuing success
senses.definition: very determined and energetic in trying to succeed, especially in business or sport
senses.definitionCN: 在争取成功时非常坚决、精力充沛，多用于商业或体育
senses.example: She is an aggressive saleswoman who calls twenty clients before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个干劲十足的销售员，中午前就给二十位客户打了电话。
senses.why: Take the hostility out of the step and what remains is pure forward drive, so the same energy is now praised instead of blamed.
senses.whyCN: 把「迈步逼近」里的敌意抽掉，剩下的就是纯粹的向前冲劲；同一股劲在这里不再被责备，反而成了褒义的「有闯劲」。

senses.title: Bold and hard-selling
senses.definition: of a marketing or sales method, bold, forceful and hard to ignore
senses.definitionCN: 指营销或推销手段大胆、强劲，让人难以忽视
senses.example: The startup grew through aggressive advertising rather than word of mouth.
senses.exampleCN: 这家初创企业靠猛烈的广告投放而不是口碑成长起来。
senses.why: Advertising that steps right up to the buyer and will not take no for an answer is the same forward step turned into a sales technique.
senses.whyCN: 广告径直走到买家面前、不肯接受拒绝，这就是把「向前迈步」做成了推销技术，所以营销语境里的强势只是同一个动作换了场地。

senses.title: Fast-spreading and hard to treat
senses.definition: of a disease or tumour, growing quickly and spreading in a way that is hard to control
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病或肿瘤发展迅速、扩散猛烈而难以控制
senses.example: Doctors found an aggressive form of cancer in his left lung.
senses.exampleCN: 医生在他的左肺发现了一种侵袭性很强的癌症。
senses.why: Medicine borrows the image of an enemy that advances without restraint: the growth attacks tissue the way an army attacks land.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了「不顾一切向前推进的敌人」这一形象：病变侵犯组织，就像军队侵占土地，因此同样的「攻击」被用来描述病情的发展速度。

senses.title: Harsh in effect
senses.titleCN: 强效的；刺激性的（化学品）
senses.definition: of a chemical or cleaning product, strong enough to damage surfaces or skin
senses.definitionCN: 指化学品或清洁剂效力强到会损伤表面或皮肤
senses.example: Do not use an aggressive cleaner on the polished stone floor.
senses.exampleCN: 不要在抛光石地面上使用强效清洁剂。
senses.why: A substance that attacks dirt without mercy also attacks the surface beneath, so the word keeps its attacking core and aims it at materials.
senses.whyCN: 毫不留情地攻击污垢的东西，也会攻击下面的表面；词义仍保留「攻击」这个核心，只是对象从人换成了材料，于是有了「强效而伤物」的意思。

senses.title: Seeking high returns at high risk
senses.definition: of an investment plan or strategy, accepting high risk in order to aim for high returns
senses.definitionCN: 指投资计划或策略为追求高回报而承担高风险
senses.example: His portfolio is too aggressive for someone close to retirement.
senses.exampleCN: 对一个快要退休的人来说，他的投资组合过于激进。
senses.why: Finance takes the forward-charging step and measures it in risk: the investor who pushes hardest for gain also stands closest to loss.
senses.whyCN: 金融把「一路向前冲」换算成风险来计量：最拼命追收益的投资者，离亏损也最近，所以这股冲劲在投资语境里被叫作「激进」。

intro.en: Aggressive comes from Latin aggredi 'to go towards, attack', built on ad- 'towards' and gradi 'to walk, step'; English took the past-participle stem aggress-.
intro.cn: aggressive 来自拉丁语 aggredi「走向、攻击」，由 ad-「朝向」与 gradi「走、迈步」构成；英语取的是它的过去分词词干 aggress-。

items.en: The verb gradi meant 'to walk, step'; the related noun gradus meant 'a step'. Both are recorded Latin words, not reconstructions.
items.cn: 动词 gradi 意为「走、迈步」，相关名词 gradus 意为「一步、台阶」；两者都是有记录的拉丁语词，不是重构形式。

items.en: Ad- 'towards' plus gradi produced aggredi, 'to go towards, approach', which already in Latin could mean 'to set upon, attack'.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 gradi 构成 aggredi，意为「走向、接近」，在拉丁语中已经可以表示「扑向、攻击」。

items.en: The past participle aggressus 'having advanced against' and the later noun aggressio 'an attack' supply the stem aggress- that English uses.
items.cn: 过去分词 aggressus「已经逼近攻击的」与后起名词 aggressio「攻击」，提供了英语所用的词干 aggress-。

items.en: English aggressive is recorded in the eighteenth century in the sense 'tending to attack'; it may have come through French agressif, and exact first dates differ between sources.
items.cn: 英语 aggressive 于十八世纪有记录，意为「有攻击倾向的」；可能经法语 agressif 传入，确切首见年代各家记载不一。

items.en: In the twentieth century, especially in American business writing, the word gained the approving sense 'energetic and enterprising', and technical uses in medicine and finance followed.
items.cn: 二十世纪，尤其在美国商业写作中，这个词获得「积极进取、有闯劲」的褒义；医学与金融的技术用法随后出现。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin root gradi 'to step'; the near-meaning group gathers words for hostility, confidence and force, each with a different tone.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁词根 gradi「迈步」构成的一族词；近义组收表示敌意、自信与强力的词，彼此语气不同。

entries.definition: The noun for an unprovoked attack, or in psychology for hostile behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「侵略、攻击行为」，心理学中也指攻击性；与 aggressive 同出拉丁语动词 aggredi。

entries.definition: The person or country that starts an attack.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「侵略者、挑衅者」，指先动手的一方，与 aggressive 共享词干 aggress-。

entries.definition: The adverb: in a hostile or forceful manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「咄咄逼人地、强势地」，由本词加后缀 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Movement forward or improvement; built on pro- 'forward' plus the same gradi.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「前进、进步」，由 pro-「向前」加同一个 gradi 构成，与 aggressive 共用「迈步」这一词根。

entries.definition: The act of going out, or a way out; e- 'out' plus the same gradi.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「外出、出口」，由 e-「向外」加同一个 gradi 构成，词根与 aggressive 相同而方向相反。

entries.definition: Unfriendly and showing dislike; it names the feeling, while aggressive names the readiness to act.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「敌对的、不友好的」，侧重心里的敌意，而 aggressive 侧重随时动手的架势。

entries.definition: Confidently stating one's views without attacking others; usually positive where aggressive is often negative.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「坚定自信的、敢于表达的」，不含攻击他人的意思，通常为褒义，而 aggressive 常带贬义。

entries.definition: Eager to fight, especially of a country or a person's tone; more formal and more clearly warlike.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「好战的、寻衅的」，多用于国家或说话语气，比 aggressive 更正式、战争意味更明确。

entries.definition: Strong and effective in action or speech, with no hint of hostility.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「强有力的、有说服力的」，只强调力量与效果，完全没有敌意。

entries.definition: Too eager to get what one wants, in a way that annoys people; informal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「爱出风头、强人所难的」，指过分急于达到目的而令人反感，属口语用词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin parts ad- and gradi, the recorded family forms, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语部件 ad- 与 gradi、有记录的词族形式，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Ad- is 'towards' and gradi is 'to step': aggressive pictures one step taken straight at someone.
normal.cn: ad- 是「朝向」，gradi 是「迈步」：aggressive 画的就是朝某人径直迈出的一步。

normal.en: The same root appears in progress and egress, one stepping forward and one stepping out.
normal.cn: 同一词根还出现在 progress 与 egress 里，一个是向前迈，一个是向外迈。

normal.en: Aggression and aggressor keep the open hostility; aggressive can also be praise for a hard-driving team.
normal.cn: aggression 与 aggressor 保留了公开的敌意，而 aggressive 也可以用来称赞一支拼劲十足的团队。

normal.en: In sales talk an aggressive campaign is one that walks right up to the buyer.
normal.cn: 在销售语境里，aggressive campaign 就是一直走到买家面前的推广。

normal.en: Medicine speaks of an aggressive tumour because it advances fast, like an army.
normal.cn: 医学说 aggressive tumour，是因为它推进得快，像一支军队。

abstract.en: Picture a person leaning forward with one foot already across the line.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人身体前倾，一只脚已经越过了界线。

abstract.en: The same step can be a fist, a sales pitch or a tumour: only the target changes.
abstract.cn: 同一个迈步动作可以是拳头、推销话术或肿瘤，变的只是对象。

abstract.en: The word is a thermometer of tone: said of an enemy it is blame, said of a sales team it is praise.
abstract.cn: 这个词像一支语气温度计：用在敌人身上是责备，用在销售团队身上就是称赞。

examples.en: The dog became aggressive whenever a stranger came near the gate.
examples.cn: 只要有陌生人靠近大门，那条狗就变得凶猛。

examples.en: The startup grew through aggressive advertising rather than word of mouth.
examples.cn: 这家初创企业靠猛烈的广告投放而不是口碑成长起来。

examples.en: Doctors found an aggressive form of cancer in his left lung.
examples.cn: 医生在他的左肺发现了一种侵袭性很强的癌症。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿格瑞西夫」——阿格往前一步、顶到你面前：好斗，也指一股往前冲的狠劲。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「朝向」加 gradi「走、迈步」构成动词 aggredi「走向、扑向、攻击」，其过去分词词干 aggress- 进入英语；本义是「朝对方迈出一步」，先有「攻击的」之义，二十世纪又长出「进取、强势」的褒义。

sensesIntro.en: Seven senses of aggressive all keep one gesture, a step taken towards someone; only the target and the judgement change: a rival, a border, a market, a tumour, a surface, a portfolio.
sensesIntro.cn: aggressive 的七个义项都保留同一个动作，即朝某人迈出一步；变的只是对象与评价：对手、边境、市场、肿瘤、材料表面、投资组合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one foot crosses a line, the body leans forward, and the step is aimed at whoever stands ahead.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚越过界线，身体前倾，这一步直指站在前面的人。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the step becomes a threat, and the word means ready to fight or quarrel.
branches.cn: 人身线：迈步变成威胁，词义就是随时准备动手或争吵。

branches.en: THE ARMY: the same step is taken by a state across a border, and it is called invasion.
branches.cn: 军队线：同一个步子由国家跨过边境来走，就叫侵略。

branches.en: THE MARKET: without hostility the step is drive, and in selling it becomes a hard push.
branches.cn: 市场线：去掉敌意，这一步就是闯劲，在推销里则成了强硬的推力。

branches.en: THE BODY: a growth that advances without restraint is described with the same word.
branches.cn: 身体线：不受约束地向前推进的病变，也用同一个词来形容。

branches.en: MATERIALS AND MONEY: the same force is measured as damage to a surface or as risk in a portfolio.
branches.cn: 材料与金钱线：同一股力量又被换算成对表面的损伤，或投资组合里的风险。

intro.en: Aggressive is a Latin prefix plus a Latin stepping root, with ordinary English endings added to build the family.
intro.cn: aggressive 由拉丁语前缀加一个表示「迈步」的拉丁词根构成，英语再添普通词尾扩展出这一词族。

latinIntro.en: Gradi, gradus, aggredi, aggressus and aggressio are all recorded in Latin, so only the deeper Indo-European root would be reconstructed, and it is not needed here.
latinIntro.cn: gradi、gradus、aggredi、aggressus 与 aggressio 在拉丁语中均有记录，因此这里不需要动用重构形式。

items.example: It gives the word a sense of direction.
items.exampleCN: 它给这个词带上方向感。

items.example: Gradi is the stepping root behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: gradi 是整个词族背后那个「迈步」的词根。

items.example: It supplies the idea of a measured step.
items.exampleCN: 它提供了「一步的距离」这一概念。

items.example: The verb already meant both approach and attack.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词当时已兼有「接近」与「攻击」两义。

items.example: English builds its adjectives on this stem.
items.exampleCN: 英语的形容词就建在这个词干上。

derivatives.zh: 与本源出拉丁语名词 aggressio，义为「侵略；攻击行为；攻击性」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「咄咄逼人地；强势地」
由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「好斗；攻击性；闯劲」
与本源出拉丁语动词 aggredi，义为「侵略者；挑衅者」

definition_zh: 以前的；前任的；前者的
definition_en: existing or happening before, holding a position before, or the first of two things mentioned
core_image: 旧照片里那栋已经拆掉的老房子
scene: 他是这家公司的前任经理。 He is the former manager of the company.
sceneCN: 这里 former 是「前任的」（第 2 个义项）；句意：他是这家公司的前任经理。

derivatives.zh: 以前
前者

senses.title: In earlier times
senses.definition: existing or happening in an earlier period
senses.definitionCN: 存在于或发生在较早时期
senses.example: The former factory is now a museum.
senses.exampleCN: 以前的工厂现在是博物馆。
senses.why: This is the broad time sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是宽泛的时间义项。

senses.title: Previous holder
senses.definition: having held a position before the present one
senses.definitionCN: 在现任之前担任过某职位
senses.example: He is the former manager of the company.
senses.exampleCN: 他是这家公司的前任经理。
senses.why: A role can be left behind.
senses.whyCN: 职位是可以被留在身后的。

senses.title: The first of two
senses.definition: the first of two things just mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 刚提到的两件事中的第一件
senses.example: Of tea and coffee, I prefer the former.
senses.exampleCN: 茶和咖啡之中，我更喜欢前者。
senses.why: A small grammatical sense with a big role.
senses.whyCN: 一个语法义项很小，作用却很大。

intro.en: Former began as a word for the first of two.
intro.cn: former 最初是表示两者中前一个的词。

items.en: Forma meant first.
items.cn: forma 意为第一。

items.en: Former meant earlier or first.
items.cn: former 意为较早的或第一的。

items.en: It came to mean previous in time.
items.cn: 它逐渐表示时间上在先的。

items.en: The phrase the former named the first of two.
items.cn: the former 用来指两者中的前者。

items.en: It also described a previous holder of a post.
items.cn: 它也用来描述曾任某职位的人。

note.en: Former is compared with similar-looking words and with words for what came before.
note.cn: 把 former 与形近词以及表示先前之事的词作比较。

entries.definition: official or ceremonial
entries.definitionCN: 正式的

entries.definition: a fixed rule or recipe
entries.definitionCN: 公式；配方

entries.definition: the arrangement of information
entries.definitionCN: 格式

entries.definition: coming before in time
entries.definitionCN: 先前的

entries.definition: existing before
entries.definitionCN: 在前的

entries.definition: happening before now
entries.definitionCN: 较早的

normalIntro.en: Former points backward at what used to be.
normalIntro.cn: former 指向身后那个曾经存在的事物。

normal.en: The former factory is now a museum.
normal.cn: 以前的工厂现在是博物馆。

normal.en: He is the former manager of the company.

normal.en: Of tea and coffee, I prefer the former.

normal.en: She met a former colleague at the station.
normal.cn: 她在车站遇到一位前同事。

normal.en: In former times, this road was a river.
normal.cn: 从前这条路是一条河。

abstract.en: The former is the shadow the present casts behind.
abstract.cn: 前者是现在投在身后的影子。

abstract.en: A former home still knows your footsteps.
abstract.cn: 旧居仍然认得你的脚步。

abstract.en: Titles change hands; the word former stays.
abstract.cn: 头衔会易主，而 former 这个词留下。

examples.en: Of tea and coffee, I prefer the former.

dict_mnemonic.text: former 来自表示「第一」的古词：两个东西里排第一的是前者，时间上排在前面的就是以前。

root: 源自古英语 forma（第一）的比较级，核心义「在时间或顺序上靠前的」。

sensesIntro.en: Former means earlier, previous in a role, or the first of two.
sensesIntro.cn: former 意为以前的、前任的或前者的。

core.en: What stands before now in time or order.
core.cn: 在时间或顺序上位于现在之前的事物。

branches.en: An old building outlives its use.
branches.cn: 老建筑比它的用途活得更久。

branches.en: A manager steps down.
branches.cn: 经理卸任了。

branches.en: Two choices put one first.
branches.cn: 两个选择让其中一个排在前面。

branches.en: Old things and old roles both remain former.
branches.cn: 旧物与旧职位都保留着 former 的身份。

branches.en: The first of two and the previous holder share the word.
branches.cn: 两者中的前者与前任共享这个词。

intro.en: Former builds a small family of past and position words.
intro.cn: former 构成表示过去与职位的词族。

latinIntro.en: Former is Germanic; Latin pristinus, former, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: former 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 pristinus（以前的）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The former owner left a note.
items.exampleCN: 前房主留下了一张便条。

items.meaning: someone who used to work with you

items.meaning: a place where one used to live

items.example: Life in former times was slower.

definition_zh: 分析；分析结果；化验；解析；精神分析；数学分析
definition_en: the process or result of separating something complex into its parts in order to understand it
core_image: 散开的零件按顺序摆回桌面，每一件的位置都看得清楚
scene: 会议室的白板上写满箭头与圈，几个人围着长桌争论数据的走向。 Her analysis of the sales figures showed where the losses had begun.
sceneCN: 这里 analysis 是「分析结果」（第 1 个义项：把整体拆开研究的过程与结论）；句意为她对销售数字的分析指出了亏损从何处开始。画面里有白板、箭头与围着长桌讨论的人。

pos.zh: 名词：分析；分析结果；化验；解析；精神分析；数学分析

derivatives.zh: 由同一希腊词族经法语进入英语的动词，义为「分析；化验」
由本词加后缀 -ist 构成，义为「分析师；化验员」
由希腊形容词词干加 -al 构成，义为「分析的；善于分析的」
由 analytical 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「以分析的方式」
由 analytic 加复数后缀构成，义为「数据分析学；分析技术」

senses.title: The process of separating a whole
senses.definition: the process of examining something complex by separating it into its parts
senses.definitionCN: 把复杂事物拆成各个部分来考察的过程
senses.example: The analysis took longer than the experiment itself.
senses.exampleCN: 分析所用的时间比实验本身还长。
senses.why: Greek analysis is a loosening: the name belongs first to the act of untying the whole.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 analysis 是「松开」，这个名字首先属于把整体解开的那件事。

senses.title: The result or written account
senses.definition: the conclusions or written account produced by such an examination
senses.definitionCN: 这种考察所得出的结论或写成的报告
senses.example: Her analysis of the sales figures showed where the losses had begun.
senses.exampleCN: 她对销售数字的分析指出了亏损从何处开始。
senses.why: The act produces a result, and the result takes the same name as the act.
senses.whyCN: 动作产生了结果，结果就沿用了动作的名字。

senses.title: Chemical testing of a substance
senses.definition: a laboratory test that identifies the components of a substance
senses.definitionCN: 在实验室检验某物质的组成成分
senses.example: A chemical analysis revealed traces of salt in the well.
senses.exampleCN: 化学分析显示井水中有盐的痕迹。
senses.why: Chemistry performs the loosening in a literal way, separating a sample into measurable components.
senses.whyCN: 化学以字面方式完成这种「拆开」，把样本分离成可测量的成分。

senses.title: A branch of mathematics
senses.definition: the branch of mathematics dealing with limits, continuity, derivatives and integrals
senses.definitionCN: 研究极限、连续性、导数与积分的数学分支
senses.example: Calculus is the first course in mathematical analysis for many students.
senses.exampleCN: 对许多学生来说，微积分是数学分析的第一门课。
senses.why: Mathematics resolves a complex function into simpler limiting parts, so the field takes the name of the resolving act.
senses.whyCN: 数学把复杂函数拆解成更简单的极限部分，因此这个领域沿用了「拆解」的名字。

senses.title: A course of psychoanalysis
senses.definition: a long course of treatment that explores unconscious thoughts and feelings
senses.definitionCN: 长期探究潜意识想法与情感的治疗过程
senses.example: He began an analysis with a therapist after the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后，他开始接受一位治疗师的精神分析。
senses.why: The mind is treated as a layered whole, and the treatment loosens those layers over time.
senses.whyCN: 心灵被当作有层次的整体，治疗则用较长时间把这些层次一层层松开。

senses.title: Grammatical parsing
senses.definition: the description of a sentence by identifying its grammatical parts
senses.definitionCN: 通过识别语法成分来描述一个句子
senses.example: A grammatical analysis of the poem opened the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 讲座以对这首诗的语法分析开场。
senses.why: A sentence is a built structure, and grammatical analysis shows its joints in order.
senses.whyCN: 句子是搭建起来的结构，语法分析按顺序展示它的接缝。

intro.en: Analysis is the noun that came first; the English verb was formed from it, not the other way round.
intro.cn: analysis 是先出现的名词，英语动词是由它造出来的，而不是反过来。

items.en: Lyein meant 'to loosen, untie', the root of a large learned family.
items.cn: lyein 意为「松开、解开」，是一大族学术词汇的词根。

items.en: Ana- 'up, throughout' plus lyein gave analyein, 'to loosen up, resolve into parts'.
items.cn: ana-「向上、彻底」加 lyein 得到 analyein，意为「松开、分解成部分」。

items.en: The noun analysis named 'a dissolving, a resolution', especially of a complex whole.
items.cn: 名词 analysis 指「分解、解析」，尤指复杂整体的拆解。

items.en: Medieval Latin adopted the Greek noun in learned and later scientific writing.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语在学术与后来的科学写作中采用了这个希腊名词。

items.en: English borrowed analysis first as a learned noun; the verb analyse followed by back-formation. Exact dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语先借入名词 analysis 作为学术用词，动词 analyse 随后由它反推而成；确切年代不确定。

items.en: The plural analyses keeps the Greek pattern, and the word now covers chemistry, grammar, mathematics and therapy.
items.cn: 复数 analyses 保留希腊语变化方式，这个词今天覆盖化学、语法、数学与心理治疗。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same family with its spelling variants; the near-meaning group gathers formal studies and summaries.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词族及其拼写变体；近义组收正式的研究与综述类词。

entries.definition: The British verb formed from the noun; American spelling is analyze.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，英式拼写 analyse，美式拼写 analyze，由本名词反推而成。

entries.definition: A person who carries out analysis, especially in finance or data work.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「分析师」，指从事分析工作的人，多用于金融或数据领域。

entries.definition: Adjective: using or showing careful analysis.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「分析的、善于分析的」，指做事有条理地拆解研究。

entries.definition: The systematic computational analysis of data, used as a plural noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「数据分析学、分析技术」，指对数据的系统计算分析。

entries.definition: A careful look or investigation, not necessarily a formal separation into parts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「检查、审查」，强调仔细查看，未必拆成部分。

entries.definition: A careful piece of research on a subject; broader and less technical than analysis.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「研究」，指对某课题的仔细探讨，范围更宽，技术性较弱。

entries.definition: A division of information into categories, often for practical display.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「分类细目、分解」，常指为展示方便而把信息分门别类。

entries.definition: A general survey or assessment rather than a detailed structural separation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「回顾、评述」，偏总体评估，而不是细致的结构拆解。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Greek noun, its irregular plural, and the scientific fields that borrowed it.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的希腊名词、它不规则的复数，以及借用它的各个科学领域。

normal.en: The plural is analyses: the Greek -is becomes -es, just as in crisis and crises.
normal.cn: 复数是 analyses：希腊语 -is 变 -es，正如 crisis 变 crises。

normal.en: The noun came before the verb; English made analyse from analysis.
normal.cn: 名词先出现，英语是从 analysis 造出 analyse 的。

normal.en: Chemical analysis separates a sample; mathematical analysis separates a function into limits.
normal.cn: 化学分析把样本分离，数学分析把函数拆成极限。

normal.en: In the final analysis is a fixed phrase meaning after everything is weighed.
normal.cn: in the final analysis 是固定短语，意为「把所有因素权衡之后」。

normal.en: Analyst and analytics both grow from this noun, one a person, one a field.
normal.cn: analyst 与 analytics 都由这个名词长出，一个指人，一个指领域。

abstract.en: Picture a machine taken apart on a cloth, every part in a neat row, the whole readable at a glance.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器在布上被拆开，每个零件排成整齐一行，整体一眼就能看懂。

abstract.en: Picture a map with layers peeled apart: roads on one sheet, rivers on another, hills on a third.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图被分成几层：道路在一张上，河流在另一张上，山丘在第三张上。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence laid out like a skeleton, its joints labelled one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象一个句子被摆成一副骨架，每一处关节都逐一标出名字。

examples.en: Her analysis of the sales figures showed where the losses had begun.
examples.cn: 她对销售数字的分析指出了亏损从何处开始。

examples.en: A chemical analysis revealed traces of salt in the well.
examples.cn: 化学分析显示井水中有盐的痕迹。

examples.en: In the final analysis, the cheaper plan was also the slower one.
examples.cn: 归根结底，更便宜的那个方案也是更慢的那个。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿拉分析」——阿拉把整台机器拆成一排零件：分析、分析结果

root: 希腊语 lyein「松开」加前缀 ana-「彻底」构成 analyein「拆解」，名词 analysis 指「分解、解析」，经中世纪拉丁语进入学术语言，再由英语借入。复数为 analyses，保留希腊语 -is 变 -es 的方式。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses share one noun of separation: the act, its result, chemical testing, a mathematical field, a therapy, and a grammatical description.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项共享同一个「拆解」名词：动作本身、动作的结果、化学化验、数学分支、一种治疗，以及语法描述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole lies in pieces on a table, each piece in its place and the structure finally visible.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个整体在桌上散成零件，每件各就其位，结构终于看清。

branches.en: THE ACT LINE: the process of taking a complex whole apart.
branches.cn: 动作线：把复杂整体拆开的过程。

branches.en: THE RESULT LINE: the conclusions or report produced by the act.
branches.cn: 结果线：动作产生的结论或报告。

branches.en: THE LABORATORY LINE: chemical analysis makes separation physical.
branches.cn: 实验室线：化学分析让「分离」成为物理动作。

branches.en: THE FORMAL LINES: mathematics and grammar each take a structure apart by rule.
branches.cn: 形式线：数学与语法各自按规则拆解一种结构。

branches.en: THE MIND LINE: psychoanalysis loosens the layers of the unconscious.
branches.cn: 心灵线：精神分析把潜意识的层次松开。

intro.en: Analysis keeps its Greek prefix, root and ending almost unchanged, which is why its plural also keeps a Greek shape.
intro.cn: analysis 几乎原样保留了希腊前缀、词根与词尾，因此它的复数也保留了希腊语形态。

latinIntro.en: Latin analysis and its adjective are documented borrowings from Greek, so the Latin layer here is recorded rather than reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 analysis 及其形容词都是有文献的希腊借词，因此这里的拉丁层次属于记录而非重构。

items.example: It completes the loosening in analysis.
items.exampleCN: 它把 analysis 中的「松开」做到彻底。

items.example: It is the root behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个名词背后的词根。

items.example: It marks the act of separation.
The noun entered English as a learned word.

items.example: It appears in analytical and analytics.

definition_zh: 商业的；营利性的；电视广告
definition_en: connected with buying and selling, made in order to earn money, or an advertisement on television or radio
core_image: 电视节目被一段广告突然打断的那三十秒
scene: 节目演到一半，屏幕切进一段广告。 The commercial broke the film into three parts.
sceneCN: 这里 commercial 指「电视广告」（第 3 个义项：插播的广告片）；句意是这段广告把影片切成了三段。

derivatives.zh: 商业；贸易
使商业化
商业上
商业主义

senses.title: Related to trade
senses.definition: connected with the buying and selling of goods and services
senses.definitionCN: 与货物和服务的买卖有关的
senses.example: The city has a large commercial district.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市有一大片商业区。
senses.why: The ending -ial turns the noun commerce into an adjective of relation.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ial 把名词 commerce 变成表示关联的形容词。

senses.title: Made to earn money
senses.definition: produced or run in order to make a profit rather than to help
senses.definitionCN: 为获取利润而非出于公益而制作或经营的
senses.example: The project was purely commercial in its aims.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目的目的纯粹是营利。
senses.why: Trade exists to make money, so the adjective also judges motives.
senses.whyCN: 买卖本就是为了赚钱，所以这个形容词也用来评判动机。

senses.title: An advertisement
senses.definition: a short advertisement on television or radio
senses.definitionCN: 电视或广播中播放的短广告
senses.example: The commercial lasted only twenty seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 这则广告只持续了二十秒。
senses.why: Broadcasters shortened the phrase commercial message into one word.
senses.whyCN: 广播机构把「商业信息」这一说法缩成了一个词。

intro.en: Commercial is commerce plus -ial, and the noun behind it means merchandise.
intro.cn: commercial 是 commerce 加 -ial 构成，其名词本义是货物交易。

items.en: Merx meant goods, and commercium meant trade.
items.cn: merx 意为货物，commercium 意为交易。

items.en: French commercial described matters of trade.
items.cn: 法语 commercial 用来描述与贸易有关的事务。

items.en: English commercial first appeared in writing about trade law.
items.cn: 英语 commercial 最早出现在关于贸易法的文字中。

items.en: It widened to banks, vehicles and anything done for profit.
items.cn: 它的范围扩展到银行、车辆以及任何以营利为目的的事物。

items.en: Radio and television gave the word its noun sense, an advertisement.
items.cn: 广播与电视赋予了它名词义，即广告。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers adjectives ending in the same sound, while the meaning group names trade words and advertisements.
note.cn: 形近组收的是结尾读音相同的形容词，近义组列出贸易词与广告词。

entries.definition: extremely important for a result
entries.definitionCN: 至关重要的

entries.definition: relating to people living together
entries.definitionCN: 社会的；社交的

entries.definition: approved by a person in authority
entries.definitionCN: 官方的；正式的

entries.definition: relating to trade and merchants
entries.definitionCN: 商业的；贸易的

entries.definition: busy with buying and selling
entries.definitionCN: 从事买卖的

entries.definition: a notice that promotes a product
entries.definitionCN: 推销产品的广告

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a street of shops, then move to the motive of profit and to the ad that interrupts a film.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一条店铺林立的街开始，再走到营利的动机与打断影片的广告。

normal.en: Commerce is the noun, commercial is the adjective, and the ad sense came later.
normal.cn: commerce 是名词，commercial 是形容词，广告义是后来才有的。

normal.en: A commercial break is literally a break paid for by traders.
normal.cn: 广告时段字面上就是商人付钱买下的间歇。

normal.en: Commercial success measures money, not quality.
normal.cn: 商业上的成功衡量的是钱，而不是质量。

normal.en: A commercial bank serves ordinary customers, not only governments.
normal.cn: 商业银行服务普通客户，而不只是政府。

normal.en: Add -ize and something becomes a business.
normal.cn: 加上 -ize，某事物就变成了一门生意。

abstract.en: Picture a street where every window is a shop window.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街，每扇窗都是橱窗。

abstract.en: Picture a film freezing while a voice praises soap.
abstract.cn: 想象影片定格，一个声音在夸肥皂。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag hanging from a painting.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅画上挂着价签。

examples.en: The commercial broke the film into three parts.
examples.cn: 这段广告把影片切成了三段。

examples.en: They turned the old house into commercial offices.
examples.cn: 他们把老房子改成了商业办公室。

examples.en: The play was a commercial success but a critical failure.
examples.cn: 这部戏在商业上成功，评价却很糟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 commercial 记成 commerce（商业）加 ial：与商业有关的，就是商业的，也指插播的广告。

root: 由 commerce 加形容词后缀 -ial 构成，词根上溯拉丁语 merx（货物）与 commercium（交易），本义是与买卖有关的。

sensesIntro.en: From anything connected with trade, to anything done for profit, and finally to the ad that pays for broadcasting.
sensesIntro.cn: 从与贸易有关，到为营利而做，再到为播出付费的广告。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a film stopped for thirty seconds while someone sells something.
core.cn: 核心意象：电视节目被一段广告突然打断的那三十秒。

branches.en: The plain trade sense is the base adjective meaning.
branches.cn: 普通的贸易义是这个词的基础形容词义。

branches.en: Profit is the purpose behind trade, so the word also judges intent.
branches.cn: 利润是贸易背后的目的，所以这个词也评判意图。

branches.en: The noun sense came from radio and television schedules.
branches.cn: 名词义来自广播与电视的节目安排。

branches.en: A commercial street and a commercial film share one motive.
branches.cn: 商业街与商业片共享同一个动机。

branches.en: An ad is the profit motive squeezed into thirty seconds.
branches.cn: 广告就是把营利动机压缩进三十秒。

intro.en: Commercial is an -ial adjective, and its family shares the root of commerce.
intro.cn: commercial 是带 -ial 的形容词，家族与 commerce 共用同一个词根。

latinIntro.en: The Latin merc- for goods also underlies merchant and market.
latinIntro.cn: 表示货物的拉丁词根 merc- 也支撑着 merchant 与 market。

items.example: The show has long commercial breaks.
items.exampleCN: 这个节目广告时段很长。

items.meaning: in terms of trade or profit
items.example: The drug is not commercially available.
items.exampleCN: 这种药在商业渠道买不到。

items.meaning: to turn something into a business
items.exampleCN: 他们把村里的节日商业化了。

items.meaning: the process of becoming a business
items.example: Critics fear the commercialization of sport.
items.exampleCN: 批评者担心体育被商业化。
这部小说抨击现代商业主义。
商业把这两个地区连在一起。

items.structure: related noun from the same root
items.example: The merchant sold spices and cloth.
items.exampleCN: 这位商人卖香料和布匹。

items.example: It is a non-commercial radio station.
items.exampleCN: 这是一家非商业性电台。

definition_zh: 反对；抗争；与……对垒；与……相对
definition_en: to speak or act against something in order to stop it, to resist a force, to compete against someone, or to stand in contrast to something
core_image: 一块木板被人从两边同时顶住，中间微微弯起，谁也没有松手
scene: 村口的广场上聚起人群，一块画着道路规划的木板靠在树上，几个人指着板子大声争论。 Most residents opposed the plan to widen the road.
sceneCN: 这里的 opposed 是「反对」（第 1 个义项：不同意并试图阻止某项计划）；句意为多数居民反对拓宽这条路的方案。图中可辨识物件：木板、树、围拢的人群。

pos.zh: 反对；抗争；与……对垒；与……相对

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁名词 oppositio 而来，词干取自 opponere 的分词，义为「反对；对立」
由拉丁语 oppositus 而来，义为「相反的；对面的」
由 oppose 加 -ing 构成，义为「对立的；反对的」
由拉丁语 opponere 的现在分词而来，义为「对手；反对者」

senses.title: To disagree with and try to stop something
senses.definition: to say or do something against a plan, idea or action in order to prevent it
senses.definitionCN: 对某项计划、主张或行动表示异议并设法阻止
senses.example: Most residents opposed the plan to widen the road.
senses.exampleCN: 多数居民反对拓宽这条路的方案。
senses.why: Latin opponere meant to place something in the way, so opposing a plan is imagined as putting an obstacle in its path.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 opponere 意为把东西挡在路上，所以反对一项计划，被想成在它的路上放一个障碍。

senses.title: To resist a powerful force or authority
senses.definition: to struggle against a government, army or other power that is stronger than you
senses.definitionCN: 与比自己更强大的政府、军队或其他力量相抗争
senses.example: The villagers opposed the dam for years without success.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们为反对这座水坝抗争多年，却没有成功。
senses.why: When the thing in the way is a whole power rather than a plan, the same verb turns from objecting into resisting.
senses.whyCN: 当挡在前面的是一整个强权而不是一份计划时，同一个动词就从「提出异议」转为「抵抗」。

senses.title: To compete against someone
senses.definition: to take part in a contest, election or game against another person or team
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、选举或对局中与另一人或另一队相争
senses.example: The two teams will oppose each other in the final.
senses.exampleCN: 两支队伍将在决赛中互相对垒。
senses.why: A contest also places two sides opposite each other, so the verb that means setting against serves games and elections as well.
senses.whyCN: 比赛同样把两边摆到彼此对面，于是这个意为「置于对面」的动词也能用于球赛和选举。

senses.title: To stand in contrast to something
senses.definition: to be set on the other side of a comparison, as in the phrase as opposed to
senses.definitionCN: 在比较中被放在另一边，如固定说法 as opposed to 所示
senses.example: The job needs patience as opposed to speed.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作要的是耐心，而不是速度。
senses.why: The verb began as a picture of two things facing each other, and comparison keeps that picture: one thing is placed against another to show the difference.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词起初是一幅两物正面对望的画面，比较正保留了这幅画：把一物置于另一物对面，以显出差别。

intro.en: Oppose came into English from Old French, which had reshaped the Latin verb opponere, to set against; the English family still keeps that image of an obstacle placed in the way.
intro.cn: oppose 由古法语进入英语，而古法语改造了拉丁语动词 opponere（置于对面）；这一族英语词仍保留「把障碍挡在路上」的画面。

items.en: The prefix ob- meant toward, against or in front of, and before p it appears as op-, as in opponere and oppose.
items.cn: 前缀 ob- 意为朝向、对着、在……之前，在 p 前写作 op-，如 opponere 与 oppose。

items.en: Ponere meant to put or place, and it stands behind a large family of English verbs about positioning.
items.cn: ponere 意为放置、摆下，是英语一大族表示「安放位置」的动词背后的词。

items.en: Ob- plus ponere gave opponere, to set against or place in the way, used of shields, arguments and rivals.
items.cn: ob- 与 ponere 合成 opponere，意为置于对面或挡在路上，盾牌、论点和对手都能用。

items.en: Old French remade the verb as opposer, meaning to set against or to object, and passed it to English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语把该动词改造成 opposer，意为置于对面或提出异议，诺曼时期之后传入英语。

items.en: Modern English uses oppose for objecting, for resisting power, for competing and for the contrast in as opposed to.
items.cn: 现代英语用 oppose 表示提出异议、抵抗强权、参与竞争，以及 as opposed to 中的对比。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin verb for placing; the near-meaning group collects verbs for standing against something or someone.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「放置」动词上的词；近义组收表示「对某事或某人站到对面」的动词。

entries.definition: The person or side that stands against you.
entries.definitionCN: 站在你对面的那个人或一方。

entries.definition: The act of resisting, or the group that resists.
entries.definitionCN: 抵抗的行为，或进行抵抗的群体。

entries.definition: Facing the other way, or as different as possible.
entries.definitionCN: 朝向另一边的，或差别尽可能大的。

entries.definition: Able to be placed against another finger, as a thumb.
entries.definitionCN: 能与别的手指对置的，如拇指。

entries.definition: To try to stop something that is pushing against you.
entries.definitionCN: 设法挡住正向你压来的东西。

entries.definition: To say that one disagrees with a plan or statement.
entries.definitionCN: 表示对某项计划或说法不赞同。

entries.definition: To refuse openly to obey a person or rule.
entries.definitionCN: 公开拒绝服从某人或某条规矩。

entries.definition: To argue that something is wrong or not true.
entries.definitionCN: 争论某事有误或不实。

normalIntro.en: Oppose keeps the Latin verb for placing under a prefix of opposition, so the hooks picture a barrier set down in front of something moving.
normalIntro.cn: oppose 在表示「对着」的前缀下保留了拉丁语「放置」动词，所以记忆钩子想的是在某物前进的路上放下一道障碍。

normal.en: The prefix is op-, the form ob- takes before p, so oppose and opponent share a beginning for the same reason.
normal.cn: 前缀是 op-，也就是 ob- 在 p 前的形式，所以 oppose 与 opponent 的开头出于同一个道理。

normal.en: Old French opposer stands between the Latin verb and the English word, which is why the spelling ends in -ose rather than -ere.
normal.cn: 古法语 opposer 夹在拉丁动词与英语词之间，所以拼写以 -ose 而非 -ere 收尾。

normal.en: Be opposed to is the passive shape of the same verb: to be placed opposite something is to hold a view against it.
normal.cn: be opposed to 是同一动词的被动形式：被摆到某物对面，也就是对它持反对看法。

normal.en: As opposed to sets two things side by side so that the difference shows, and it keeps the original picture of facing.
normal.cn: as opposed to 把两样东西并排摆出，让差别显形，保留的正是「面对面」的原画面。

normal.en: Opposed takes a single s while the base oppose has a double p, so check both letters when writing the forms.
normal.cn: opposed 只有一个 s，而原形 oppose 是双 p，书写这些形式时两组字母都要留意。

abstract.en: To oppose is to put your weight on one side of a board and hope the other side gives way first.
abstract.cn: 反对就是把重量压到木板的一边，指望另一边先让步。

abstract.en: The same verb covers a spoken objection and a long resistance, because both begin by standing in the way.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词既指一句口头异议，也指长年的抵抗，因为两者都从「挡在路上」开始。

abstract.en: A comparison is a quiet form of opposition: nothing is fought, but two things are still placed face to face.
abstract.cn: 比较是一种安静的对抗：没有争战，但两样东西仍被摆成面对面。

examples.en: Most residents opposed the plan to widen the road.
examples.cn: 多数居民反对拓宽这条路的方案。

examples.en: She is strongly opposed to any change in the schedule.
examples.cn: 她强烈反对对日程作任何改动。

examples.en: The job needs patience as opposed to speed.
examples.cn: 这份工作要的是耐心，而不是速度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「偶剖事」——偶一剖开事情的原委，就有人站出来反对；记住 oppose 是反对、抗争。

root: 来自古法语 opposer，再上溯拉丁语 opponere（置于对面），由 ob-（对着、在前，在 p 前变 op-）与 ponere（放置）合成。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a barrier placed in the way; the senses divide by what stands on the other side, a plan, a power, a rival team, or a point of comparison.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是挡在路上的一道障碍；义项按对面是什么分出：一份计划、一股强权、一支对手队伍，或一个比较项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a board held from both sides at once, bending slightly in the middle, with neither hand letting go.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块木板被人从两边同时顶住，中间微微弯起，谁也没有松手。

branches.en: neighbours pointing at a road plan on a board
branches.cn: 邻居们指着木板上的道路方案

branches.en: villagers standing before a rising dam
branches.cn: 村民站在渐渐升高的大坝前

branches.en: two teams walking onto the same field
branches.cn: 两支队伍走进同一片场地

branches.en: patience set beside speed in one sentence
branches.cn: 同一句话里并排放着的耐心与速度

branches.en: the same verb for a loud objection and a quiet contrast
branches.cn: 同一个动词，既指高声异议，也指无声对照

intro.en: The word is a Latin compound of a prefix meaning against and the verb for placing, reshaped by French and fitted with English endings.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中「对着」前缀与「放置」动词的复合词，经法语改造，再接上英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere, opponere and oppositus are recorded, so this family has a reliable Latin ancestry and a clear picture of something set in the way.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ponere、opponere、oppositus 均有记录，因此这一族英语词有可靠的拉丁语世系，也有清晰的「某物被挡在路上」的画面。

items.meaning: able to be placed against another part

definition_zh: 稳定的；稳固的；马厩；牛棚；把（马）拴入马厩
definition_en: firmly fixed and not likely to move or change, or a building where horses are kept
core_image: 四条腿踏实的马厩与站稳不晃的马——一切都立得牢
scene: 雨后的农场里，木门吱呀作响。 The farmer led the tired horse back into its warm stable for the night.
sceneCN: 这里 stable 是「马厩」（第 5 个义项：养马的建筑物）；句意为农夫把疲惫的马牵回温暖的马厩过夜。

pos.zh: 形容词：稳定的；稳固的；沉稳的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「稳定性；稳固」
由本词加动词后缀构成，义为「使稳定；使平稳」
由 un- 加本词构成，义为「不稳定的；动摇的」
由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「稳固地」

senses.title: Firmly fixed, not moving
senses.definition: physically firm and not likely to fall or move
senses.definitionCN: 物理上牢固，不易倒下或移动
senses.example: Make sure the ladder is stable before you climb.
senses.exampleCN: 爬梯子前先确认它放稳了。
senses.why: A thing that stands on a wide base holds still.
senses.whyCN: 立足面宽的东西站得稳。

senses.title: Not changing or likely to change
senses.definition: staying at the same level or state over time
senses.definitionCN: 长时间保持同一水平或状态
senses.example: The country enjoyed stable prices for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家多年来物价平稳。
senses.why: What holds still physically also holds still in numbers and moods.
senses.whyCN: 物理上不动的，在数字与情绪上也不动摇。

senses.title: Calm and sensible in character
senses.definition: having a calm, reasonable personality that does not swing suddenly
senses.definitionCN: 性格沉着理性，不会突然波动
senses.example: She is the most stable member of the team.
senses.exampleCN: 她是队里最沉稳的人。
senses.why: A steady person is a steady building among people.
senses.whyCN: 沉稳的人如同人群中一栋不晃的建筑。

senses.title: Chemically or medically not changing
senses.definition: not likely to break down, react, or worsen, as a compound or a patient
senses.definitionCN: 化合物不易分解反应，或病人病情不再恶化
senses.example: The patient is now in a stable condition.
senses.exampleCN: 病人目前情况稳定。
senses.why: Science borrows the standing-still image for matter and bodies.
senses.whyCN: 科学把「站立不动」的意象借给物质与身体。

senses.title: A building for horses
senses.definition: a building where horses are kept and fed
senses.definitionCN: 养马、喂马的建筑物
senses.example: There are twelve stalls in the new stable.
senses.exampleCN: 新马厩里有十二个栏位。
senses.why: The same Latin root meant a standing place for animals.
senses.whyCN: 同一拉丁词根本指牲口站立安顿之处。

senses.title: The horses owned or trained together
senses.titleCN: 统指一家的马匹；赛马群体
senses.definition: all the racehorses belonging to one owner or trainer
senses.definitionCN: 属于同一主人或训练师的全部赛马
senses.example: The champion horse is the pride of his stable.
senses.exampleCN: 这匹冠军马是马房引以为傲的宝贝。
senses.why: The building stands for everything kept inside it.
senses.whyCN: 建筑物代指其中饲养的一切。

senses.title: To put a horse into a stable
senses.definition: to keep a horse in a stable, especially for the night
senses.definitionCN: 把马安置在马厩中，尤指过夜
senses.example: The riders stabled their horses and went to dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 骑手们把马拴进马厩后去吃饭。
senses.why: Putting the horse where it stands still gives the verb.
senses.whyCN: 让马站定安顿，便有了这个动词。

intro.en: Stable the adjective and stable the barn are two different words: one from Latin stabilis "able to stand", one from Latin stabulum "a standing place".
intro.cn: 形容词 stable 与马厩 stable 是两个词：一个来自拉丁语 stabilis「能站立的」，一个来自 stabulum「牲口站立之所」。

items.en: A root meaning "to stand" underlies both words; the reconstruction is generally accepted.
items.cn: 表示「站立」的词根是两词共同基础；这一重构被普遍接受。

items.en: Latin stabilis meant "able to stand, firm"; stabulum meant "a stall or standing place for animals".
items.cn: 拉丁语 stabilis 意为「能站立、牢固」；stabulum 意为「牲口的栏厩」。

items.en: Old French gave English both estable "firm" and estable "barn".
items.cn: 古法语将 estable「牢固」与 estable「厩栏」一并传入英语。

items.en: The two homonyms settled in Middle English with different spellings in time.
items.cn: 两个同形词进入中古英语，拼写逐渐分化。

items.en: The adjective grew scientific senses, the noun grew the racing sense and the verb.
items.cn: 形容词发展出科学义项，名词发展出赛马义与动词用法。

note.en: Stable pairs with its opposite unstable, and the horse-barn word shares spelling with the firm word.
note.cn: stable 与反义词 unstable 成对，而马厩义与牢固义同形。

abstract.cn: 感受一张怎么靠都不晃的桌子。

abstract.en: Picture a line on a graph going flat and staying flat.

examples.en: After the storm the old bridge was still stable.
examples.cn: 暴风雨后那座老桥依然稳固。

latinIntro.en: Latin stabilis and stabulum share the stand-root stare, which also gives us stay and state.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 stabilis 与 stabulum 共享表「站立」的 stare 词根，该词根也给了我们 stay 与 state。

definition_zh: 家伙；男人；小伙子
definition_en: a man, especially one that the speaker finds ordinary or likeable
core_image: 一个再普通不过的男人：蹲在路边修自行车，裤脚沾着机油
scene: 修车铺里，几个熟客围着那个蹲在地上给链条上油的男人说笑。 The mechanic who fixes bicycles in the alley is a friendly bloke.
sceneCN: 这里 bloke 是「家伙、男人」（第 1 个义项：一个普通的男性）；句意是巷子里修自行车的那个机修工是个友善的家伙。

senses.title: A man, an ordinary male person
senses.definition: a man, especially one seen as ordinary, everyday, or easy to like
senses.definitionCN: 一个男人，尤指看起来普通、日常、让人容易有好感的男性
senses.example: He seemed like a decent bloke when we met at the pub.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在酒馆见面时，他看上去像个正派的家伙。
senses.why: The word began as slang for a stranger whose name nobody knew, then settled into a warm label for any man on the street.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是指说不上名字的陌生男人，后来固定成对街头任何男性的一种带着好感的通俗称呼。

senses.title: A fellow of the speaker's own sort
senses.titleCN: 同类人；自己圈子里的人
senses.definition: a fellow belonging to the same group or sharing the speaker's way of life
senses.definitionCN: 与说话人同处一个圈子、生活方式相近的同伴
senses.example: The players welcomed the new bloke into the dressing room.
senses.exampleCN: 队员们把新来的这位迎进了更衣室。
senses.why: Because it names an unnamed male, it naturally marks him as one of us rather than an outsider.
senses.whyCN: 正因为它指「叫不上名字的男人」，它天然带有「自己人」的意味，把对方划进说话人的圈子里。

senses.title: A man referred to without naming him
senses.titleCN: 某个男人（不知名或懒得点名）
senses.definition: some man the speaker mentions without giving his name or identity
senses.definitionCN: 说话人提起来但不说出姓名或身份的某个男人
senses.example: Some bloke left his umbrella on the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 有个家伙把伞落在了公交车上。
senses.why: The vague origin of the word itself made it perfect for pointing at vague men.
senses.whyCN: 这个词自身的来历本就模糊，恰好适合用来指代身份不明的男人。

senses.title: Blokes as a collective, men in general
senses.definition: men in general, treated as a group, often contrasted with women
senses.definitionCN: 泛指男性群体，常与女性相对而提
senses.example: Down the pub, the blokes talk football all night.
senses.exampleCN: 在酒馆里，男人们整晚都在聊足球。
senses.why: Once the word means any man, the plural slides from individuals to men as a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 一旦单词可以指任何男人，复数形式便从一个个个体滑向「男人这个群体」。

senses.title: An Australian or British everyman hero
senses.titleCN: 普通人形象（澳、英文化中的平民典型）
senses.definition: in Australian and British culture, the image of the plain, honest, unpretentious man
senses.definitionCN: 在澳大利亚和英国文化中，指朴实、直率、不装腔作势的平民男子形象
senses.example: The advertisement showed a cheerful bloke in a flannel shirt.
senses.exampleCN: 广告里是一个穿法兰绒衬衫的开朗汉子。
senses.why: Cultures that prize egalitarianism turned the casual word into a positive emblem of ordinariness.
senses.whyCN: 崇尚平等的文化把这个随口的词变成了代表平凡本色的正面符号。

senses.title: A character type in fiction or comedy
senses.titleCN: 角色类型（文艺作品中的憨厚男人）
senses.definition: a stock character in stories or comedy, a plain man coping with everyday trouble
senses.definitionCN: 小说或喜剧中的一种固定角色：一个应付日常琐事的憨直男人
senses.example: The sitcom's main bloke keeps burning his own toast.
senses.exampleCN: 这部情景喜剧的主角总是把自己家的吐司烤糊。
senses.why: The warm, unglamorous flavor of the word suits comic characters built on ordinariness.
senses.whyCN: 这个词亲切而不光鲜的味道，正好契合以平凡制造笑点的喜剧角色。

senses.title: A boyfriend or husband in casual talk
senses.definition: in casual British speech, a woman's boyfriend or husband mentioned offhandedly
senses.definitionCN: 英式口语中，女性随口提到的男朋友或丈夫
senses.example: She brought her bloke to the family dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 她把男朋友带来了家宴。
senses.why: Pointing at a man without naming him works naturally for the man in one's life.
senses.whyCN: 既然可以不点名地指一个男人，那么拿来随口称呼自己生命里那个男人也十分顺口。

senses.title: Emphatic or ironic use for any person facing trouble
senses.titleCN: 强调或反讽用法（指遭遇麻烦的任何人）
senses.definition: used emphatically or ironically for anyone caught in an awkward situation, regardless of gender nuance
senses.definitionCN: 以强调或反讽口吻指陷入尴尬处境的任何人，性别色彩淡化
senses.example: Poor bloke, he locked himself out again.
senses.exampleCN: 这可怜的家伙，他又把自己锁在门外了。
senses.why: The affectionate tone lets speakers extend sympathy to anyone, male or not.
senses.whyCN: 亲切的语气让说话人可以把这份同情延伸到任何人身上，性别色彩因此淡出。

intro.en: Bloke is a nineteenth-century British slang word whose origin remains genuinely uncertain; several rival hypotheses exist and none has been proven.
intro.cn: bloke 是十九世纪的英国俚语，来源至今确实不确定；存在几种相互竞争的假说，均未被证实。

items.en: First recorded in British slang around the 1840s, meaning a man whose name is unknown, an outsider, a stranger.
items.cn: 约在十九世纪四十年代首次见于英国俚语，指叫不上名字的男人、外来者、陌生人。

items.en: One widely repeated account links it to Shelta, the cant of Irish Travellers; the link is plausible but not proven.
items.cn: 一种流传较广的说法把它与爱尔兰游居者的隐语 Shelta 联系起来；这一关联合理但未被证实。

items.en: Another hypothesis derives it from a Romani word for a man; scholars treat this as speculative.
items.cn: 另一说认为它源自某个吉卜赛语（罗姆语）中表示「男人」的词；学界视之为推测。

items.en: The word spread to Australia, where it gained a warm, egalitarian flavor and became a cultural emblem of the ordinary man.
items.cn: 这个词传入澳大利亚，带上亲切、平等的意味，成为平民男子形象的文化符号。

items.en: In twentieth-century Britain the harsh early sense faded, leaving a friendly everyday word for any man.
items.cn: 二十世纪的英国，早期生硬的「外来者」义逐渐消退，留下对任何男人的日常亲切称呼。

items.en: Today bloke is chiefly British and Australian colloquial usage; American English prefers other words for the same idea.
items.cn: 如今 bloke 主要用于英式和澳式口语；美式英语表达同样意思时更常用其他词。

note.en: Bloke has no known relatives, so the look-alike group gathers casual male-nouns from Britain and America, and the near-meaning group gathers everyday words for men.
note.cn: bloke 没有已知的同族词，形近一组收录英美口语中的男性称呼，近义一组收录表示男人的日常词汇。

entries.definitionCN: 块状物；街区；只是拼写与 bloke 相近，词源不同

entries.definitionCN: 金发的；形近但词源不同，blonde 来自法语

entries.definition: an informal word for a man, common in American English

entries.definition: a man, slightly old-fashioned and friendly in tone

entries.definition: a British word for a man, now somewhat old-fashioned and polite
entries.definitionCN: 家伙；英式用语，如今略显老派而有礼貌感

normalIntro.en: Five honest ways to remember bloke, none of them pretending to be etymology.
normalIntro.cn: 五种朴素的记忆法；它们只是联想，不是词源考证。

normal.en: bloke sounds like "block"; picture a man sitting on a block of stone in the street.
normal.cn: bloke 与 block（块）发音相近：想象一个男人蹲在街头的一块石墩上。

normal.en: b + loke: he locks his bike, a very ordinary thing a very ordinary man does.
normal.cn: b + lock（锁）：他锁上自行车，普通人常做的普通事。

normal.en: the plural blokes rhymes with folks; blokes are just folks who are men.
normal.cn: 复数 blokes 与 folks（人们）押韵：blokes 不过是「人们」中的男性。

normal.en: British sitcoms are full of blokes; recall any comic character you have seen.
normal.cn: 英式情景喜剧里满是 bloke：回忆你见过的任何一个憨直男角色。

normal.en: o in bloke is round like a friendly face; the word itself carries warmth.
normal.cn: bloke 中的 o 圆圆的像一张友善的脸；这个词自带亲切感。

abstract.en: Picture an ordinary man fixing a bicycle, oil on his hands, smiling.
abstract.cn: 想象一个普通男人在修自行车，手上沾着机油，面带微笑。

abstract.en: Think of the feeling of calling someone by no name at all, just warmly.
abstract.cn: 体会那种不叫名字、只是亲切地称呼一个人的感觉。

abstract.en: Link the word to the smell of a pub: wood, beer, and easy laughter.
abstract.cn: 把这个词和酒馆的气味连起来：木头、啤酒和轻松的笑声。

examples.en: The plumber who fixed our sink was a friendly bloke.
examples.cn: 来修水池的水管工是个友善的家伙。

examples.en: Some bloke on the train gave up his seat for the old lady.
examples.cn: 火车上有个家伙给老太太让了座。

examples.en: British comedies often show a bloke struggling with ordinary life.
examples.cn: 英式喜剧常常刻画与平凡生活较劲的男人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不乐哥」——那个不太爱笑的家伙蹲在路口修车，路过的街坊都喊他「不乐哥」，可喊多了他自己也乐了。

root: 来源不确定。一般认为 bloke 于十九世纪四十年代出现在英国俚语中，可能源自爱尔兰游居者隐语 Shelta，或与罗姆语中表示「男人」的词有关，均属假说，不可当作定论。

sensesIntro.en: From an unnamed stranger to a warm everyday label, the word now covers any man, the group of men, a cultural type, and even affectionate or ironic uses.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个叫不上名字的陌生人出发，这个词如今可以指任何男人、男人群体、文化中的平民形象，甚至带亲切或反讽色彩的随口称呼。

branches.cn: 同情或反讽延伸到陷入麻烦的任何人
