senses.example: Rain drummed on the tin roof.
senses.exampleCN: 雨点敲打铁皮屋顶。
senses.why: The metal's protective job names the coated sheet.
senses.whyCN: 锡的防锈职责命名了镀锡铁皮。

senses.title: A sealed container for food
senses.definition: an airtight metal container with a lid, holding food or drink
senses.definitionCN: 带盖密封、盛放食品饮料的金属容器
senses.example: He bought a tin of peaches.
senses.exampleCN: 他买了一罐桃子罐头。
senses.why: The container is named by the metal it is made from.
senses.whyCN: 容器以制作它的金属命名。

senses.title: A baking or loaf mould
senses.definition: a metal mould used for baking bread, cakes or pies
senses.definitionCN: 烤面包、蛋糕或派用的金属模具
senses.example: Grease the loaf tin before pouring the batter.
senses.exampleCN: 倒面糊之前先给面包模抹油。
senses.why: The same metal shapes the container and the mould.
senses.whyCN: 同一种金属既做容器也做模具。

senses.title: The contents of a tin
senses.definition: the amount or contents of one container
senses.definitionCN: 一罐所装的量或内容
senses.example: Add a tin of chopped tomatoes to the pan.
senses.exampleCN: 往锅里加一罐番茄碎。
senses.why: The vessel extends to what it holds.
senses.whyCN: 容器延伸到它所盛的东西。

senses.title: Cheap or flimsy, of machines or things
senses.definition: describing something cheaply made or sounding thin and metallic
senses.definitionCN: 形容做工廉价，或声音单薄如金属
senses.example: The old car had a tinny engine note.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆旧车引擎声单薄刺耳。
senses.why: The base metal becomes a byword for cheapness.
senses.whyCN: 这种廉价金属成了廉价的代名词。

senses.title: Tin as money-slang
senses.definition: informal use for a cash box or small savings tin
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法，指钱盒或攒钱罐
senses.example: The holiday money sits in a tin on the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 度假的钱存在架子上的储蓄罐里。
senses.why: A closed metal box keeps coins the way tins keep food.
senses.whyCN: 封闭的铁盒存钱，正如铁罐存食物。

senses.title: Tin plated surfaces and small wares
senses.definition: utensils or small items made of tin or plated with it
senses.definitionCN: 锡制或镀锡的小器皿和物件
senses.example: Antique tin cups lined the dresser.
senses.exampleCN: 梳妆台上摆着一排旧锡杯。
senses.why: The metal names the ware made of it.
senses.whyCN: 金属的名字落在用它做成的器物上。

intro.en: Tin is one of the oldest metal words in English, from Old English tin, shared with Germanic cousins and known to Latin as stannum in alloys.
intro.cn: tin 是英语最古老的金属词之一，出自古英语 tin，与日耳曼诸语同源；拉丁语合金义作 stannum。

items.en: The metal was mined early and the name spread across Germanic tongues.
items.cn: 锡开采极早，其名称在日耳曼诸语中传播。

items.en: Tin named both the metal and things made of it.
items.cn: 古英语 tin 兼指金属与锡器。

items.en: Tin foil and tinsmith appear as crafts of the metal.
items.cn: 中古英语出现 tinfoil 与 tinsmith 等锡工艺词。

items.en: The sealed food tin spread with canning technology.
items.cn: 十八世纪随罐装技术普及密封食品罐。

items.en: A tin came to mean the contents as well as the can.
items.cn: 十九世纪英国用法中 tin 兼指罐中之物。

items.en: Modern British keeps tin where American English prefers can.
items.cn: 现代英式英语保留 tin，美式英语多用 can。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alike short -in words; the second sorts container neighbours.
note.cn: 第一组是 -in 结尾的形近短词；第二组列出容器义的近邻。

entries.definition: a container for rubbish or storage
entries.definitionCN: 垃圾箱；储物箱

entries.definition: a small pointed metal fastener
entries.definitionCN: 大头针；别针

entries.definition: very small in size; spelled close but a different word
entries.definitionCN: 极小的；拼写相近而非同词

entries.definition: the American word for a sealed metal food container
entries.definitionCN: 罐头（美式说法）

entries.definition: a metal mixed of two or more elements, such as bronze
entries.definitionCN: 合金，如青铜

entries.definition: metal rolled into very thin sheets for wrapping
entries.definitionCN: 箔；薄片金属

normalIntro.en: Real links: a tin of soup, tin foil, a baking tin, and a tinny sound.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：一罐汤、锡箔、烤模，以及单薄刺耳的声音。

normal.en: Tin is the pale metal that keeps steel from rust.
normal.cn: tin 是让钢板不生锈的浅色金属。

normal.en: A tin of soup is the can named after its metal.
normal.cn: 一罐汤就是以金属命名的罐头。

normal.en: Tin foil wraps lunch; the name stays even when it is aluminium.
normal.cn: 锡箔包午餐；如今多是铝箔，名字却没变。

normal.en: A baking tin shapes the loaf before the oven does.
normal.cn: 烤模在进烤箱前就定好了面包的形状。

normal.en: A tinny speaker sounds like metal hammered thin.
normal.cn: 劣质喇叭的声音像被锤薄的铁皮。

abstract.en: Every tin guards what is inside from the air.
abstract.cn: 每个罐子都替里面的东西挡住空气。

abstract.en: The cheapest metal earns a name for the humblest things.
abstract.cn: 最便宜的金属为最卑微的器物命名。

abstract.en: A tin box of coins is a pantry for tomorrow.
abstract.cn: 存钱罐是给明天预备的食品柜。

examples.en: She emptied a tin of beans into the pot.
examples.cn: 她把一罐豆子倒进锅里。

examples.en: Bronze replaced pure tin tools long ago.
examples.cn: 青铜早已取代纯锡工具。

examples.en: The wind rattled the tin roof all night.
examples.cn: 风整夜吹得铁皮屋顶作响。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「听」——敲一敲铁皮罐，「听」那空空的回响，正是 tin 罐头 → tin 锡；罐头

root: 单一词干：古英语 tin「锡」，源自原始日耳曼语，与德语 Zinn 同源；拉丁语称合金中的锡为 stannum（stannous 一词之源）。

sensesIntro.en: Tin begins as a pale metal and grows into coated sheets, sealed cans, moulds and a byword for cheapness.
sensesIntro.cn: tin 从浅色金属出发，长成镀锡铁皮、密封罐头、烤模，以及廉价的代名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pale protective metal shaped into boxes for keeping things.
core.cn: 核心意象：浅色而具保护性的金属，被做成保存东西的匣子。

branches.en: The element itself, soft and silver-white.
branches.cn: 元素本身，柔软银白。

branches.en: Coated sheets and small wares of the metal.
branches.cn: 镀锡铁皮与锡制小器物。

branches.en: The sealed can and what it holds.
branches.cn: 密封罐与罐中之物。

branches.en: The mould that shapes bread and cake.
branches.cn: 定形面包蛋糕的模具。

branches.en: Cheapness by word, and coins in a box.
branches.cn: 廉价的比喻与盒中硬币。

intro.en: Tin is a native metal stem; its items show compounding and small suffixes.
intro.cn: tin 是本土金属词干；条目展示复合与小后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin name for tin is stannum; English keeps it only in chemical terms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的锡作 stannum；英语只保留在化学术语中。

items.meaning: made of tin, or thin and metallic in sound
sealed in a can; British for canned
thin metal sheet for wrapping food
a tool for cutting open cans
a worker who makes things of tin
items.example: The tinsmith made a new lantern.
items.exampleCN: 白铁匠打了一盏新灯笼。

items.example: Line the baking tin with paper.

items.meaning: inability to hear differences in music or language
items.meaningCN: 五音不全；听不出语调差异
items.example: He has a tin ear for poetry.

items.meaning: of tin with a lower valence, in chemistry
items.example: Stannous chloride is a lab reagent.

definition_zh: 年长的；上了年纪的；老年人
definition_en: rather old, used politely of people past middle age, or the group of old people as a whole
core_image: 公园长椅上，一位老人把围巾又拢紧了些
scene: 长椅上那位老人扶着扶手才站起来，动作很慢。 An elderly man rose slowly from the bench.
sceneCN: 这里 elderly 是「年长的」（第 1 个义项：客气地指已过中年、年纪较大的人）；句意是一位年长的男士慢慢从长椅上站起来。

pos.zh: 形容词：年长的；上了年纪的（较礼貌）
名词：the elderly 老年人（集合）

forms.label: 比较级（形容词，多音节用 more）
最高级（形容词，多音节用 most）

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉 -ly 得到，义为「年长的；长辈」
由 elderly 加 -ness 构成，义为「年长；老年」

senses.title: Rather old, said politely
senses.definition: past middle age and getting old, used as a polite word instead of old
senses.definitionCN: 已过中年、渐渐年老，用作 old 的客气说法
senses.example: An elderly man rose slowly from the bench.
senses.exampleCN: 一位年长的男士慢慢从长椅上站起来。
senses.why: Elderly is elder plus -ly, and elder is the comparative of old: it says older, gently, without the bluntness of old.
senses.whyCN: elderly 是 elder 加 -ly，而 elder 是 old 的比较级：它温和地说「更年长」，没有 old 那么直白。

senses.title: Old people as a group
senses.definition: with the, old people considered as a group in society
senses.definitionCN: 与 the 连用，指社会中作为一个群体的老年人
senses.example: The clinic offers free transport for the elderly.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为老年人提供免费接送。
senses.why: An adjective with the can name a whole class, so the elderly means all who answer to that description.
senses.whyCN: 形容词加 the 可以指整个类别，所以 the elderly 就是所有符合这个描述的人。

senses.title: Old and worn, said with a smile
senses.definition: used humorously of things that are old and worn out
senses.definitionCN: 戏谑地用于年久失修、老旧的物件
senses.example: My elderly laptop takes ten minutes to start.
senses.exampleCN: 我那台老掉牙的笔记本要十分钟才启动。
senses.why: The polite word for old people is transferred to machines, and the politeness itself becomes the joke.
senses.whyCN: 这个对人客气的词被挪到机器上，那份客气本身就成了笑话。

intro.en: Elderly is elder plus -ly; elder is the old comparative of old, from Old English eldra, and still carries the sense of seniority.
intro.cn: elderly 是 elder 加 -ly；elder 是 old 的古老比较级，来自古英语 eldra，至今仍带「辈分较长」的意味。

items.en: The reconstructed adjective meant old or grown up.
items.cn: 重构形容词意为「年老的、长成的」。

items.en: Eldra was the comparative of eald, old, and meant older.
items.cn: eldra 是 eald（老）的比较级，意为「更年长的」。

items.en: Elder kept the sense of senior in age or rank, especially within a family.
items.cn: elder 保留年龄或辈分较长的意思，尤用于家族内部。

items.en: The ending -ly softened the adjective into a polite description of age.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把这个形容词软化，成为对年龄的客气描述。

items.en: The elderly settled as a collective name, and the word spread jokingly to worn objects.
items.cn: the elderly 固定为集合称谓，这个词又戏谑地扩展到破旧物件上。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the elder family; the near-meaning group separates old, senior and aged by tone.
note.cn: 形近组收 elder 词族；近义组按语气区分 old、senior 与 aged。

entries.definition: Older, especially of a relative or a person of authority in a community.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词兼名词，义为「年长的；长辈」，是本词的词基。

entries.definition: The oldest of a group, usually of brothers or sisters.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最年长的」，多指兄弟姐妹中的老大。

entries.definition: Having lived a long time; plainer and blunter than elderly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「老的」，比 elderly 更直白。

entries.definition: Older or higher in rank, often used in official contexts such as senior citizens.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「年长的、资深的」，常用于 senior citizens 等正式说法。

entries.definition: Very old; it can sound more formal or more pointed than elderly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「年迈的」，比 elderly 更正式或更强调。

entries.definition: Growing old, said of a process rather than a person's state.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「老龄化的」，描述过程而非人的状态。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from elder as the gentle comparative of old, then follow the word into a group name and a joke about machines.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从 elder 这个温和的比较级出发，再走到群体称谓与关于机器的玩笑。

normal.en: Elderly is elder plus -ly: the polite way of saying older.
normal.cn: elderly 是 elder 加 -ly：说「更年长」时的客气说法。

normal.en: Old can sting; elderly steps back and leaves room.
normal.cn: old 可能刺人；elderly 往后退半步，留出余地。

normal.en: The elderly are not one person but a whole group.
normal.cn: the elderly 不是一个人，而是一整群人。

normal.en: My elderly laptop is a joke: the politeness is the point.
normal.cn: my elderly laptop 是个玩笑：那份客气本身就是笑点。

normal.en: Elderly usually starts around retirement age, old goes further.
normal.cn: elderly 大约从退休年龄起算，old 还要再往后。

abstract.en: Picture a slow rise from a park bench, hands on the armrest.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人双手扶着扶手，从公园长椅上慢慢起身。

abstract.en: The same politeness can cover a person, a group, or a tired machine.
abstract.cn: 同一份客气可以覆盖一个人、一群人，或一台疲惫的机器。

abstract.en: Elderly is old with a hand held out.
abstract.cn: elderly 就是伸出手扶一把的 old。

examples.en: An elderly man rose slowly from the bench.
examples.cn: 一位年长的男士慢慢从长椅上站起来。

examples.en: The clinic offers free transport for the elderly.
examples.cn: 这家诊所为老年人提供免费接送。

examples.en: My elderly laptop takes ten minutes to start.
examples.cn: 我那台老掉牙的笔记本要十分钟才启动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「埃尔德利」——老人扶着扶手，才慢慢站起来

root: elderly 由 elder 加 -ly 构成；elder 是 old 的古老比较级（古英语 eldra），故本词字面即「更年长的」，语气比 old 委婉。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of elderly: politely old, old people as a group, and humorously worn out.
sensesIntro.cn: elderly 的三个义项：客气地说年长、作为群体的老年人，以及戏称物件老旧。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old person rising slowly from a bench, one hand on the armrest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位老人扶着扶手，从长椅上慢慢起身。

branches.en: THE PERSON: past middle age, described politely.
branches.cn: 人物线：已过中年，用客气的方式描述。

branches.en: THE CLASS: with the, all such people together.
branches.cn: 群体线：加 the 指所有这样的人。

branches.en: THE JOKE: the same politeness spent on a tired laptop.
branches.cn: 玩笑线：同一份客气用在一台疲惫的笔记本上。

branches.en: THE TONE: the word's gentleness is what joins person and group.
branches.cn: 语气线：这个词的温和把个人与群体连在一起。

branches.en: THE TRANSFER: respect for age becomes mock respect for age in objects.
branches.cn: 转移线：对年岁的敬重变成对物件年岁的假敬重。

intro.en: Elderly is a native English adjective built on the old comparative elder with the ending -ly.
intro.cn: elderly 是英语本土形容词，由古老比较级 elder 加词尾 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are Germanic and recorded in Old English, so no Latin entry is claimed here.
latinIntro.cn: 两个构件都属于日耳曼语且在古英语中有记录，因此这里不列拉丁语条目。

items.example: It is the positive form behind elder.
items.exampleCN: 它是 elder 背后的原级。

items.example: It is the source of elder.
It is the base of elderly.

年长；老年

definition_zh: 日益；愈加；日趋
definition_en: more and more as time passes
core_image: 台阶一级一级往上，每一级都比前一级更高
scene: 这几年，很多事都在悄悄变得更难。 Students are increasingly worried about finding work.
sceneCN: 这里 increasingly 是「越来越」（第 1 个义项：随时间推移程度加深）；句意是学生们越来越担心找工作。

forms.label: 无变化（副词无词形变化）

derivatives.zh: 义为「增加、增长」，是本词的动词基础
义为「不断增加的」
义为「越来越少地」，与本词相反

senses.title: More and more over time
senses.titleCN: 越来越：随时间不断加深
senses.definition: used with an adjective to show that a quality grows over time
senses.definitionCN: 与形容词连用，表示某种性质随时间不断增强
senses.example: Students are increasingly worried about finding work.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们越来越担心找工作。
senses.why: The -ly adverb keeps the growth of increase and turns it into a rising curve beside another word.
senses.whyCN: -ly 副词保留了 increase 的「生长」义，并把它变成紧挨另一个词的上升曲线。

senses.title: Used of a trend, not a single step
senses.titleCN: 日益：用于趋势而非单次变化
senses.definition: describing a gradual shift observed across a period rather than one event
senses.definitionCN: 描述在一段时期内观察到的渐变，而非单次事件
senses.example: The city has become increasingly quiet at night.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市夜里变得日益安静。
senses.why: A single change is described by increase, but only a long drift earns the adverb.
senses.whyCN: 单次变化用 increase 就够，只有长期漂移才配得上这个副词。

senses.title: Used for growing degree in an argument
senses.titleCN: 愈加：在论述中强调程度递进
senses.definition: used to stress that one statement matters more as the argument goes on
senses.definitionCN: 用于强调随着论述推进，某一说法愈发重要
senses.example: It is increasingly hard to defend that view.
senses.exampleCN: 那种观点越来越难以辩护。
senses.why: Writers borrow the adverb to let a claim sound like an approaching tide.
senses.whyCN: 写作者借用这个副词，让论断听起来像渐渐逼近的潮水。

intro.en: Increasingly is increase with the adjective ending -ing and the adverb ending -ly added in Modern English.
intro.cn: increasingly 是 increase 加形容词词尾 -ing、再加副词词尾 -ly 构成的现代英语派生词。

items.en: Crescere, to grow, gave increscere, to grow into.
items.cn: crescere「生长」生出 increscere「长起来」。

items.en: The verb encresen entered English from French.
items.cn: 动词 encresen 由法语进入英语。

items.en: The present participle increasing began to work as an adjective.
items.cn: 现在分词 increasing 开始充当形容词。

items.en: Adding -ly produced the adverb in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 加 -ly 后，这个副词在十九世纪成型。

items.en: Modern journalism made it a standard word for trends.
items.cn: 现代新闻写作让它成为描述趋势的常用词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the increase stem; the near-meaning group holds adverbs of worsening degree.
note.cn: 形近组共用 increase 词干；近义组收表示程度加深的副词。

entries.definition: To become larger in amount.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「增加」，是本词的基础。

entries.definition: Becoming larger over time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不断增加的」。

entries.definition: Less and less as time passes.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「越来越少地」。

entries.definition: Slowly over a period of time.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「逐渐地」，重在慢。

entries.definition: In stages, step by step.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「逐步地」，重在分阶段。

entries.definition: Used with comparatives to mean always more.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，与比较级连用表示「越来越」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the staircase image, the -ly adverb slot and the trend word of news writing.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借台阶意象、-ly 副词位置与新闻里的趋势表达。

normal.en: Increase plus -ing plus -ly: a growth that never finishes and only describes another word.
normal.cn: increase 加 -ing 再加 -ly：一个永不结束的生长，只用来修饰别的词。

normal.en: It almost never stands alone; it leans on an adjective such as difficult or important.
normal.cn: 它几乎不单独站立，总倚着一个形容词，如 difficult 或 important。

normal.en: If one step is a jump, this word describes the whole staircase.
normal.cn: 如果一步是跳跃，这个词描述的是整座楼梯。

normal.en: Decrease the first letter and the direction of the staircase reverses.
normal.cn: 把首字母换一换，楼梯的方向就反过来。

normal.en: News headlines love it because it reports a drift without naming a cause.
normal.cn: 新闻标题偏爱它，因为它只报道漂移，不指明原因。

abstract.en: Slow change is the only kind the naked eye cannot catch while it happens.
abstract.cn: 缓慢的变化是唯一在发生当下无法被肉眼捕捉的变化。

abstract.en: To say increasingly is to admit that no single instant can show the shift.
abstract.cn: 说「越来越」，等于承认没有任何一个瞬间能显示这次转变。

abstract.en: The adverb measures direction, while the reader still has to guess the speed.
abstract.cn: 这个副词只测方向，速度仍要读者自己去猜。

examples.en: Housing in the city is becoming increasingly expensive.
examples.cn: 这座城市的住房越来越贵。

examples.en: People increasingly work from home.
examples.cn: 人们越来越多地在家办公。

examples.en: It is increasingly rare to see a public phone.
examples.cn: 公共电话越来越少见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印快格林里」——印得越来越快，纸一摞摞往格林里堆。

root: 拉丁语 crescere（生长）→ increscere → increase；加 -ing、-ly 构成 increasingly。

sensesIntro.en: Increasingly takes the growth inside increase and turns it into an adverb that always leans on another word and reports a long drift.
sensesIntro.cn: increasingly 把 increase 里的生长变成副词，它总要倚着另一个词，报道的是一段漫长的漂移。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a staircase whose every step is higher than the last.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座每级都比上一级更高的楼梯。

branches.en: QUALITY LINE: a quality deepens beside an adjective.
branches.cn: 性质线：某种性质在形容词旁边加深。

branches.en: PERIOD LINE: the change is spread across years.
branches.cn: 时段线：变化摊展在数年之间。

branches.en: ARGUMENT LINE: a claim gains force as the case goes on.
branches.cn: 论述线：说法随着论证推进而更有力。

branches.en: RHYTHM LINE: the word marks direction, not speed.
branches.cn: 节奏线：这个词标方向，不标速度。

branches.en: TONE LINE: writers use it to sound calm about bad news.
branches.cn: 语气线：写作者用它把坏消息说得平静。

intro.en: A growth root with a participial ending and an adverb ending stacked on top.
intro.cn: 一个「生长」词根上依次叠加分词词尾与副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin crescere, to grow, gave increscere; English added -ing and -ly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crescere「生长」生出 increscere，英语再加上 -ing 与 -ly。

definition_zh: 声称；断言；索取；认领；主张；权利要求
definition_en: to say that something is true when others may doubt it, to ask for something as your right, or a right that you say you have
core_image: 一只手举着一张写有自己名字的单据
scene: 保险员把表格推过来，笔尖停在签名处。 Two men claim the same wallet at the front desk.
sceneCN: 这里 claim 指「认领」（第 2 个义项：主张某物归自己所有）；句意是两个男人在前台都声称那个钱包是自己的。

derivatives.zh: 索赔人；申请人
取回；开垦；回收
免责声明；否认

senses.title: To state as true
senses.definition: to say that something is true when other people may not believe it
senses.definitionCN: 在别人可能不相信时仍说某事为真
senses.example: She claims the keys were left on the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 她声称钥匙是落在桌子上的。
senses.why: The old verb meant to cry out, so a claim is something said loudly and publicly.
senses.whyCN: 这个古老动词本指大声喊出，因此 claim 是被大声公开说出来的话。

senses.title: To demand as your own
senses.definition: to ask for something that you believe belongs to you by right
senses.definitionCN: 要求得到你认为按权利属于自己的东西
senses.example: He claimed his luggage at the counter.
senses.exampleCN: 他在柜台认领了自己的行李。
senses.why: A public cry for something became a formal demand for property or payment.
senses.whyCN: 公开喊出某物，演变成对财产或款项的正式要求。

senses.title: A right or a demand
senses.definition: a statement that you have a right to something, or that right itself
senses.definitionCN: 关于你有权得到某物的声明，或该项权利本身
senses.example: Her claim to the land was never proved.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这块土地的所有权主张从未得到证实。
senses.why: The noun took the same shape as the verb and named the demand rather than the act of demanding.
senses.whyCN: 名词与动词同形，但它指所提的要求，而不是提出要求的动作。

intro.en: Claim comes from a Latin verb meaning to cry out, which also gave English exclaim and proclaim.
intro.cn: claim 出自拉丁语中表示大声喊出的动词，exclaim 与 proclaim 也来自它。

items.en: Clamare meant to cry out or call loudly.
items.cn: clamare 意为大声喊叫或呼喊。

items.en: Clamer carried the sense of calling out a demand.
items.cn: clamer 带有喊出一项要求的含义。

items.en: English took the word as claimen in law and argument.
items.cn: 英语以 claimen 的形式把它用于法律与辩论。

items.en: A claim became a formal demand for land or money.
items.cn: claim 成为对土地或金钱的正式要求。

items.en: The verb widened to plain statements of fact.
items.cn: 这个动词扩展到对事实的普通陈述。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short words with a similar shape, while the meaning group holds verbs of saying and demanding.
note.cn: 形近组列出外形相近的短词，近义组列出言说与要求类动词。

entries.definition: a tool that holds things tightly together
entries.definitionCN: 把东西紧紧夹住的工具

entries.definition: to hold something firmly with your hand
entries.definitionCN: 用手紧紧握住某物

entries.definition: to praise someone loudly and publicly
entries.definitionCN: 公开大声地赞扬某人

entries.definition: to state something firmly as a fact
entries.definitionCN: 坚定地把某事说成事实

entries.definition: to announce something officially or clearly
entries.definitionCN: 正式或清楚地宣布某事

entries.definition: to ask for something very firmly
entries.definitionCN: 非常强硬地要求某物

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the cry-out root, the legal demand and the noun-verb pair.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用呼喊词根、法律要求以及名动同形这三条线。

normal.en: Claim belongs with exclaim and proclaim; all three contain the Latin cry for a call.
normal.cn: claim 与 exclaim、proclaim 同族，三者都含拉丁语表示喊叫的部分。

normal.en: To claim is to put your hand up in public, either to speak or to take.
normal.cn: claim 就是在公开场合举手，要么发言，要么拿东西。

normal.en: The noun and the verb look the same, so a claim is both the act and the thing demanded.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形，所以 claim 既是动作，也是所要求的对象。

normal.en: Insurance papers are full of claims, because a claim asks for money.
normal.cn: 保险文件里满是 claim，因为这个词可以指索赔。

normal.en: Lay claim to is the fixed phrase for ownership, not for an opinion.
normal.cn: lay claim to 是表示所有权的固定说法，不用来说看法。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised at an auction with a numbered card.
abstract.cn: 想象拍卖会上举起一只拿着号牌的手。

abstract.en: Picture a luggage tag matching the name on a passport.
abstract.cn: 想象一张行李牌与护照上的名字对得上。

abstract.en: Picture a boundary line drawn on a map and then disputed.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上画出一条边界线，随后被人争执。

examples.en: She claims the keys were left on the desk.
examples.cn: 她声称钥匙是落在桌子上的。

examples.en: He claimed his luggage at the counter before the taxi came.
examples.cn: 出租车来之前，他在柜台认领了行李。

examples.en: The company made a claim for the damaged goods.
examples.cn: 公司就受损货物提出了索赔。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cl 想成「喊」，aim 想成「目标」：朝着目标喊一声，就是声明这东西归我。

root: 源自拉丁语 clamare（大声喊叫），经古法语 clamer 进入英语，本义是喊出自己的权利。

sensesIntro.en: A loud cry turns into an assertion, then into a demand, and finally into the right behind the demand.
sensesIntro.cn: 一声大喊先变成断言，再变成索求，最后变成索求背后的权利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised hand holding a paper with a name on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只举起的手拿着写有名字的纸。

branches.en: The old cry becomes a public statement of fact.
branches.cn: 古老的呼喊变成公开的事实陈述。

branches.en: The same cry becomes a request for what is yours.
branches.cn: 同样的呼喊变成对属于自己之物的索求。

branches.en: The noun names the demand and the right behind it.
branches.cn: 名词指所提的要求以及其背后的权利。

branches.en: Saying and taking share one verb because both are public acts.
branches.cn: 言说与索取共用一个动词，因为两者都是公开行为。

branches.en: A claim needs a right, and a right survives only if claimed.
branches.cn: 索求需要权利，而权利只有被主张才存在。

intro.en: One short verb grows a plural, two participles, an agent noun and two prefixed forms.
intro.cn: 一个短动词长出复数、两个分词、一个施动名词和两个前缀形式。

latinIntro.en: The base clamare also underlies exclaim, proclaim and acclaim, all built with Latin prefixes.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 clamare 也是 exclaim、proclaim、acclaim 的来源，这些词都加了拉丁语前缀。

items.meaning: to state true or demand as a right
items.example: He will claim the seat by the window.

items.meaning: the verb with a single subject
items.example: She claims to know the answer.
They claimed the land in court.
items.exampleCN: 他们在法庭上主张这块土地。

items.example: He is claiming the reward today.

items.meaning: a person who makes a claim

items.example: They reclaimed the field from the sea.
items.exampleCN: 他们围海造出了那片田。

items.example: The site carries a short disclaimer.
items.exampleCN: 这个网站附有一份简短免责声明。

latinEntries.example: Clamare gave English claim and exclaim.
latinEntries.exampleCN: clamare 给了英语 claim 与 exclaim。

definition_zh: 投掷；抛；（板球等的）球场；音高；推销；（船的）颠簸；沥青（名词）
definition_en: to throw something, or the level of a sound, a playing field, a sales talk, or a black sticky substance
core_image: 手臂一扬把球掷出——同样的动作在球场、音高、推销和沥青上各掷一次
scene: 投手咬着嘴唇看了一眼本垒，手臂一扬把球掷了出去。 The pitcher gave the ball a fast pitch toward the plate.
sceneCN: 这里是「投掷」（第 1 个义项：一次投球的动作）；句意为投手把球快掷向本垒板。画面就是那记干脆的投球。

pos.zh: 投掷；抛；搭（帐篷）；定调；推销
投掷；球场；音高；推销词；沥青

derivatives.zh: pitch 加 -er 构成的施动名词，义为「投手；水罐」
由 pitcher 与 plant 合成，义为「猪笼草；瓶子草」
pitch 的动名词，义为「投掷；（船）纵向颠簸」

senses.title: To throw something
senses.definition: to throw something with force, or to aim it at a target
senses.definitionCN: 用力扔出某物，或朝目标掷去
senses.example: He pitched the crumpled letter into the bin.
senses.exampleCN: 他把揉皱的信扔进垃圾桶。
senses.why: The basic arm-throwing action is the seed; every later sense plants this throw somewhere else.
senses.whyCN: 最基本的挥臂投掷是种子；后面的义项都把这记投掷种到别处。

senses.title: To fix a tent or camp
senses.definition: to set up a tent in a place
senses.definitionCN: 在某处支起帐篷
senses.example: We pitched our tent on the ridge before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 天黑前我们在山脊上搭好了帐篷。
senses.why: Stakes are driven and lines thrown across the ground, so pitching a camp repeats the throw in pegs and ropes.
senses.whyCN: 打桩、甩绳，扎营的每个动作都是一次投掷的重演。

senses.title: The level of a sound
senses.definition: how high or low a musical note or voice is
senses.definitionCN: 乐音或嗓音的高低程度
senses.example: Her voice dropped to a lower pitch.
senses.exampleCN: 她的嗓音降到更低的音高。
senses.why: A thrown object rises and falls in an arc; a voice thrown into the air lands at a certain height.
senses.whyCN: 掷出的物体划出弧线；抛向空中的嗓音也落在一个高度上。

senses.title: A playing field
senses.definition: a marked area of ground on which a sport is played, used especially in British English
senses.definitionCN: 划好界线的运动场地，尤用于英式英语
senses.example: The fans poured onto the pitch after the final whistle.
senses.exampleCN: 终场哨响后球迷涌进球场。
senses.why: The game is pitched onto this square of ground, the same directed throw applied to the playing area itself.
senses.whyCN: 比赛被「掷」上这块场地，定向的投掷挪到了场地本身。

senses.title: A sales talk
senses.definition: a planned talk meant to persuade someone to buy or agree
senses.definitionCN: 为说服他人购买或同意而设计的说辞
senses.example: He gave his pitch in ten sentences and closed the deal.
senses.exampleCN: 他用十句话讲完推销词，签下了合同。
senses.why: The seller throws his offer at the buyer like a ball aimed at the strike zone.
senses.whyCN: 卖方像投手瞄准好球区一样，把自己的提议掷向买方。

senses.title: The rise and fall of a ship
senses.definition: the movement of a ship or aircraft when the front rises and falls
senses.definitionCN: 船或飞机的头部起伏的运动
senses.example: The storm made the ferry pitch heavily.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴让渡轮颠簸得厉害。
senses.why: The bow rises and falls like an object thrown in an arc, so the motion borrowed the throw's name.
senses.whyCN: 船头像被抛出的物体一样起落，这种运动便借了投掷的名字。

senses.title: A black sticky substance
senses.definition: a thick black sticky substance made from tar, used for waterproofing
senses.definitionCN: 由焦油制成的黑色黏稠物质，用于防水
senses.example: The hull was sealed with pitch before the voyage.
senses.exampleCN: 出海前船壳用沥青封了缝。
senses.why: Pitched wood was thrown in the fire to make waterproof tar; the substance kept the old past-participle name.
senses.whyCN: 把劈开的木头（pitched wood）扔进火里熬出防水焦油，这种物质便沿用了那个过去分词的名字。

intro.en: English pitch is two words sharing one spelling: a Germanic verb of throwing, and an English past participle turned noun for tar.
intro.cn: 英语的 pitch 是两个词共用一个拼法：一个日耳曼源的投掷动词，和一个由过去分词转成名词的焦油词。

items.en: The throwing verb goes back to a reconstructed Germanic root for stabbing or fixing, related to picking.
items.cn: 投掷动词源自一个表示「刺、钉牢」的重构日耳曼词根，与 pick 同源。

items.en: Pitch appeared in Middle English as a verb for throwing and driving in stakes.
items.cn: 中古英语中 pitch 已作动词，指投掷和打桩。

items.en: The substance sense comes from Old English pic, the past participle of piccan, to pitch wood for tar.
items.cn: 物质义来自古英语 pic，即 piccan（劈木熬焦油）的过去分词。

items.en: Sport, sound, sales and ship motion each extended the throw image from the Middle Ages onward.
items.cn: 从中世纪起，体育、声音、推销与船的颠簸各自延伸了投掷意象。

items.en: Modern use keeps all strands alive, from football pitches to elevator pitches.
items.cn: 现代用法把各条线都留着，从足球场到电梯推销词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers pitch's family and look-alikes; the near-meaning group gathers throws, fields and sound levels.
note.cn: 形近组收 pitch 词族与形近词；近义组收投掷、场地与音高词。

entries.definition: The player who throws the ball, and the jug he is named after.
entries.definitionCN: 投手，也指投手一词所借用的水罐。

entries.definition: A small piece of material or ground; spelled one vowel away from pitch.
entries.definitionCN: 补丁；小块地；与 pitch 仅差一个元音字母，词源不同。

entries.definition: A thin rod or a device that turns power on and off; rhymes with pitch.
entries.definitionCN: 细枝或电源开关；与 pitch 押韵，词源无关。

entries.definition: The general word for sending something through the air by hand.
entries.definitionCN: 用手把东西抛向空中的通称。

entries.definition: A light, careless throw, often upward.
entries.definitionCN: 轻轻随意的一抛，常向上。

entries.definition: The marked area for tennis or basketball, the American sibling of pitch.
entries.definitionCN: 网球场或篮球场，是 pitch 在美式英语中的对应词。

normalIntro.en: All senses hang on one arm-throw; remember the throw and the rest follow.
normalIntro.cn: 所有义项都挂在一次挥臂投掷上；记住这记投掷，其余随之而来。

normal.en: One throw, seven lands: the bin, the campsite, the voice, the field, the deal, the ship, the tar.
normal.cn: 一掷七落：垃圾桶、营地、嗓音、球场、生意、船身、焦油。

normal.en: Pitch black is as dark as the tar sense of the word.
normal.cn: pitch black 与该词的焦油义一样黑。

normal.en: The pitcher of water and the pitcher of baseball share one family tree.
normal.cn: 水罐和棒球投手同属一棵家谱树。

normal.en: A sales pitch throws the deal at you; catch it or duck.
normal.cn: 推销词把生意掷向你；接住，或者躲开。

normal.en: High pitch is a note thrown high into the air.
normal.cn: 高音是被高高抛进空中的音符。

abstract.en: An arm swings back, then whips forward — the whole word lives in that swing.
abstract.cn: 手臂后摆再猛然前挥——整个词都活在这一挥里。

abstract.en: A ship's bow lifting and dropping on grey waves, again and again.
abstract.cn: 船头在灰浪上一起一落，反复不止。

abstract.en: Black tar bubbling in a fire of split wood, sealing the seams of a hull.
abstract.cn: 劈开的木头在火里熬出冒泡的黑焦油，封住船壳的缝。

examples.en: Pitch the ball to me and I'll catch it.
examples.cn: 把球抛给我，我来接。

examples.en: The singer hit every note at exactly the right pitch.
examples.cn: 歌手把每个音都唱在准确的音高上。

examples.en: Her pitch for the new app won over the investors.
examples.cn: 她对新应用的推销打动了投资人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「劈瞧」——一球劈手掷出，瞧它落在球场还是音阶；pitch 就是掷。

root: pitch（投掷义）源于日耳曼语系表示「刺、钉」的动词（中古英语 picchen），与 pick 相关；pitch（沥青义）来自古英语 pic，是 piccan（劈木熬焦油）的过去分词；两词拼法巧合重合。

sensesIntro.en: One throwing arm explains a battlefield of meanings: the ball, the tent, the note, the field, the deal, the ship and the tar.
sensesIntro.cn: 一条挥掷的手臂解释了一片意义战场：球、帐篷、音符、场地、生意、船身与焦油。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arm throwing something with force toward a chosen spot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条手臂用力把某物掷向选定的地点。

branches.en: the letter tossed into the bin
branches.cn: 扔进垃圾桶的信

branches.en: tent ropes thrown across the grass
branches.cn: 甩过草地的帐篷绳

branches.en: a note landing at its height
branches.cn: 落在某一高度的音符

branches.en: the offer hurled at the buyer
branches.cn: 掷向买方的提议

branches.en: the arc of a throw and the arc of a ship's bow
branches.cn: 投掷的弧线与船头的弧线

intro.en: Pitch carries no productive affixes; its family is built from conversion, compounds and one agentive suffix.
intro.cn: pitch 没有能产性词缀；词族靠转类、复合和一个施动后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Germanic roots dominate; Latin contributes nothing to this word family.
latinIntro.cn: 日耳曼词根主导；拉丁语在这个词族里毫无贡献。

definition_zh: 运动；移动；动作；手势；动议；提议；机械运转；排便；用手势示意
definition_en: the act or process of moving, or a movement of the hand that signals something, or a formal proposal put to a meeting
core_image: 一枚棋子被手指从棋盘一格推到下一格，棋后拖出一道浅痕
scene: 会议开到一半，有人从座位上站起，把一页提案放到桌上，请全场表决。 She rose to put a motion to the committee.
sceneCN: 这里 motion 指提交会议表决的正式提议（第 3 个义项：动议）；句意：她起身向委员会提出一项动议。图中可辨识物件：提案纸页、会议桌、木槌、座位牌；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 运动；移动；手势；动议；机械运转

derivatives.zh: 静止的；不动的
静止；不动
运动的；与运动有关的

senses.title: Change of position
senses.definition: the process of changing position or place over time
senses.definitionCN: 随时间改变位置或处所的过程
senses.example: The motion of the pendulum is regular and easy to time.
senses.exampleCN: 钟摆的运动很规律，容易计时。
senses.why: Latin motio is simply a moving, from movere 'to move'; this is the plainest and oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 motio 就是「移动」，出自 movere「移动」；这是最直白、最古老的义项。

senses.title: A gesture that carries a message
senses.definition: a movement of the hand or head used instead of words to signal something
senses.definitionCN: 代替言语、用来示意的手部或头部动作
senses.example: With a quick motion of his hand, the conductor silenced the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 指挥手一挥，大厅便静了下来。
senses.why: A gesture is a small movement that does the work of a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 手势是一个小动作，却承担了一句话的功能。

senses.title: A proposal put to a meeting
senses.definition: a formal proposal presented at a meeting for discussion and a vote
senses.definitionCN: 在会议上正式提出、供讨论并表决的提议
senses.example: The motion to extend the deadline was carried by nine votes.
senses.exampleCN: 延长截止日期的动议以九票通过。
senses.why: To bring something forward is to move it onto the table; the proposal is the thing set in motion before the room.
senses.whyCN: 把某事提出来，就是把它移到桌面上；提议就是被推到全场面前的东西。

senses.title: A request made to a court
senses.titleCN: 向法庭提出的程序申请
senses.definition: a formal request asking a court to make a ruling or take an action
senses.definitionCN: 请求法庭作出裁定或采取行动正式申请
senses.example: The defence filed a motion to dismiss the charge.
senses.exampleCN: 辩方提交了撤销指控的动议。
senses.why: A court, like an assembly, decides only what is moved before it, so the legal request kept the parliamentary name.
senses.whyCN: 法庭和议会一样，只裁决被推到它面前的事，因此法律申请沿用了议会里的名称。

senses.title: The act of starting a process
senses.definition: the act of setting a plan, process or event going
senses.definitionCN: 使计划、进程或事件开始运转的动作
senses.example: One phone call set the whole rescue in motion.
senses.exampleCN: 一个电话启动了整场救援。
senses.why: The fixed phrase set in motion treats a process as a body that must be pushed before it will move.
senses.whyCN: 「使……启动」这一固定说法把进程当作一具必须先推一把才会动的身体。

senses.title: The running of a machine
senses.definition: the working movement of a machine or mechanism, or its state of running
senses.definitionCN: 机器或机构的运转动作，或其正在运行的状态
senses.example: The old lift was in motion again after the belt was replaced.
senses.exampleCN: 换过皮带后，老电梯又运转起来。
senses.why: A machine is a body whose parts move, so its operation is naturally called motion.
senses.whyCN: 机器是一具有部件在动的身体，因此它的运行自然被叫作 motion。

senses.title: The moving works inside a device
senses.definition: the assembly of moving parts inside a device, especially a clock or watch
senses.definitionCN: 装置内部由运动部件组成的机构，尤指钟表机芯
senses.example: A watchmaker cleaned the motion and oiled each pivot.
senses.exampleCN: 钟表匠清理了机芯，并给每个轴心上了油。
senses.why: Watchmakers named the works by the movement they produce, and the term became the trade word for the whole mechanism.
senses.whyCN: 钟表匠以它所产生的运动来命名这套机构，这个说法后来成了整个机芯的行业词。

senses.title: To signal with the hand
senses.definition: to make a movement of the hand or head as a sign or direction
senses.definitionCN: 用手部或头部的动作作为信号或指引
senses.example: The usher motioned us toward the side door.
senses.exampleCN: 引座员示意我们往侧门走。
senses.why: The noun became a verb: to give a motion with the hand is to motion someone.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：用手给出一个动作，就是向某人示意。

intro.en: Motion comes through Old French from Latin motio, a moving, built on the past-participle stem mot- of movere 'to move'. The proposal sense grows from bringing something forward, not from physical travel.
intro.cn: motion 经古法语来自拉丁 motio「移动」，由 movere「移动、推动」的过去分词词干 mot- 构成。动议义由「把某事提出来、推到面前」引申，并非来自物理位移。

items.en: Movere meant to move, to push away, to set in motion; its past-participle stem mot- is the base of the noun.
items.cn: movere 意为移动、推开、使动起来；它的过去分词词干 mot- 是名词的底子。

items.en: Motio, motionis named a moving or a movement; it is a third-declension noun built on the same stem.
items.cn: motio、motionis 指一次移动或运动；这是由同一词干构成的第三变格法名词。

items.en: Old French motion carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first as movement and soon after as a proposal.
items.cn: 古法语 motion 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，先指移动，不久也指提议。

items.en: English motion is recorded from the fourteenth century in the plain sense of movement, and in legal use soon afterwards.
items.cn: 英语 motion 自十四世纪有「移动」的直白用法记录，随后不久进入法律语境。

items.en: The sense of a proposal grows from the idea of bringing something forward, a motion made in a room rather than in space.
items.cn: 「提议」义从「把某事提出来」这一想法长出，是在房间里而非空间中做出的动作。

items.en: The first dates of the parliamentary and legal senses are approximate; the noun is well attested from the medieval period.
items.cn: 议会义与法律义的最早记录年代为约数；这个名词在中世纪已有充分记录。

note.en: The first group shares the stem of moving; the second group separates motion from a gesture, a proposal and a trend.
note.cn: 第一组共享「移动」的词干；第二组把 motion 与手势、提议、趋势等相邻说法区分开。

entries.definition: The verb and a common noun for a single act of moving; motion is the more formal noun of the process.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，也作普通名词指一次移动；motion 是更正式、指整个过程的名词。

entries.definition: From mot- plus -ive: the reason that moves a person to act, not the act of moving.
entries.definitionCN: 由「移动」词干加表倾向的词尾构成：推动人去行动的理由，不是移动的动作。

entries.definition: Built on the same stem with an agent ending: the thing that produces movement, as an engine does.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干加表施动者的词尾：产生运动的东西，如发动机。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus motion: a confused rushing about of people, a movement that is noisy.
entries.definitionCN: 表「一起」的拉丁前缀加「移动」：人群慌乱地涌动，一种喧闹的移动。

entries.definition: Not a form of motion and from a different source: it comes from a separate Latin noun for an instant or a weight, and in English it names a point in time rather than a movement.
entries.definitionCN: 不是 motion 的一种形式：它来自另一个拉丁名词，指瞬间或重量；英语中它指时间上的一点，而非移动。

entries.definition: Movement in general, often of a group or a trend; motion is more often a single act or a formal proposal.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指运动，常指一群人的行动或趋势；motion 更常指单次动作或正式动议。

entries.definition: A deliberate movement of the body that communicates; motion can be any movement, gesture is always meaningful.
entries.definitionCN: 有传达作用的身体动作；motion 可以是任何动作，gesture 一定带有意义。

entries.definition: A plan offered for consideration; a motion is a proposal put formally to a meeting.
entries.definitionCN: 提出供考虑的计划；motion 是正式提交会议表决的提议。

entries.definition: The ability to move from place to place, used of animals and vehicles rather than of processes.
entries.definitionCN: 从一处到另一处移动的能力，多用于动物与交通工具，而非抽象过程。

entries.definition: The speed at which something moves; motion names the fact of moving, not how fast.
entries.definitionCN: 移动的快慢；motion 说的是「在动」这件事，不涉及快慢。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Movere is Latin for move, and mot- is its participle stem.
normal.cn: movere 是拉丁语「移动」，mot- 是它的分词词干。

normal.en: The family runs motion, motionless, motive, motor, commotion.
normal.cn: 同族词有 motion、motionless、motive、motor、commotion。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the everyday senses: in motion, slow motion, set in motion, motion picture.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出日常义：在运动中、慢动作、启动、电影。

normal.en: Law says a motion to dismiss is a formal request, not a physical move.
normal.cn: 法律上的「撤销动议」是正式申请，不是物理移动。

normal.en: Physics describes motion with velocity and acceleration, two ways of measuring how it changes.
normal.cn: 物理用速度与加速度描述运动，这是衡量它如何变化的两种方式。

abstract.en: Picture a chess piece sliding one square, leaving a pale trail behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚棋子滑过一格，身后留下一道浅痕。

abstract.en: Picture a hand lifted at a meeting, and the room falling silent before a word is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象会议上一只手抬起，还没开口，全场就静了。

abstract.en: Picture a key turned in a lock and a whole machine waking up.
abstract.cn: 想象钥匙在锁里一转，整台机器醒了过来。

examples.en: The motion of the tide is charted twice a day.
examples.cn: 潮水的运动每天被记录两次。

examples.en: Her motion to reopen the case was rejected.
examples.cn: 她要求重审此案的动议被驳回了。

examples.en: The camera records motion in the dark by sensing heat.
examples.cn: 这台摄像机在黑暗中靠感热来记录运动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mo（摸）+ tion（神）」——摸一下就走，身子一动；motion 运动、动议

root: 拉丁 movere「移动、推动」→ 过去分词词干 mot- → 拉丁 motio「移动」→ 古法语 motion → 英语 motion；会议动议义由「提出、推动」引申。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one push: a body changes place, a hand makes a sign, an idea is pushed before a meeting, a request before a court, a process is started, a machine runs, its works are named, and finally the hand itself becomes a verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「推」展开：身体换位、手做出信号、想法被推到会议前、申请被推到法庭前、进程被启动、机器运转、机芯得名，最后手本身变成动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger pushes a piece from one square to the next, and the piece leaves a trail.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指把棋子从一格推到下一格，棋子拖出一道痕迹。

branches.en: THE PLAIN MOVE: a body changes place, and one small move of the hand carries a message.
branches.cn: 直白的动：身体换位，而手的一个小动作传达信息。

branches.en: BROUGHT BEFORE OTHERS: the same push places a proposal before a meeting or a request before a court.
branches.cn: 推到众人面前：同一个推力把提议放到会议前，或把申请放到法庭前。

branches.en: SET GOING: a process is pushed into motion, and a machine keeps moving once it starts.
branches.cn: 使之启动：进程被推入运动，机器一旦启动便持续运转。

branches.en: THE WORKS: the parts that carry the movement inside a watch take the name of movement itself.
branches.cn: 机芯：钟表内部承担运动的那套部件，直接以「运动」命名。

branches.en: THE VERB: the hand that made the sign becomes the act of motioning.
branches.cn: 动词：做出信号的那只手，变成「示意」这个动作。

intro.en: Motion is a Latin noun of moving, and the stem mot- builds verbs, agents and a whole English family.
intro.cn: motion 是表示「移动」的拉丁名词，词干 mot- 还构成动词、施动者名词与整个英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere gives motio and motion, and also motive, motor, commotion and momentum; the ending -tion names an action or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 movere 衍生 motio 与 motion，也衍生 motive、motor、commotion 与 momentum；后缀 -tion 表示动作或结果。

items.example: The root supplies the push behind every sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根为每个义项提供「推」的底子。

items.example: The Latin noun names the act of moving.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词指移动这一动作。

items.example: She rose to put a motion to the committee.
items.exampleCN: 她起身向委员会提出动议。

items.example: The cat lay motionless under the chair.
items.exampleCN: 猫一动不动地躺在椅子下。

items.example: A commotion broke out at the gate.

items.meaning: a reason that moves a person

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀
items.example: The ending turns a verb of moving into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「移动」的动词变成名词。

latinEntries.meaning: to move, push, set in motion

definition_zh: 试验；试用；审判；审讯
definition_en: a test of something to see whether it works, or the formal hearing of a case in a court
core_image: 一辆贴着彩条的车在试验场上绕圈，工程师盯着屏幕记数据
scene: 试验场上有一辆涂着彩条的车，工程师坐在场边的帐篷里看屏幕。 The new engine is still on trial before it goes on sale.
sceneCN: 这里 trial 是「试验；试用」（第 1 个义项：为检验效果而进行的测试）；句意为这款新发动机在上市前仍在试用测试中。贴着彩条在场上绕圈的车，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: trial 的词根，义为「尝试；审判」
由 try 与 out 复合，义为「选拔；试用」
由 try 加 -ing 构成，义为「令人恼火的；艰难的」

senses.title: The test run
senses.definition: an act of testing something over a period to see how well it works
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内测试某物效果如何的行为
senses.example: The new engine is still on trial before it goes on sale.
senses.exampleCN: 这款新发动机在上市前仍在试用测试中。
senses.why: The ending -al turns the verb try into a noun, and the oldest sense is the testing of something.
senses.whyCN: -al 后缀把动词 try 变为名词，最古老的含义就是检验某物。

senses.title: The day in court
senses.definition: the formal examination of a case by a judge and often a jury
senses.definitionCN: 由法官及常设陪审团对案件进行的正式审理
senses.example: The trial lasted three weeks and ended with a verdict.
senses.exampleCN: 这场审判持续了三周，以裁决结束。
senses.why: A court also tests the facts of a case, so the legal hearing borrowed the same word as the engine test.
senses.whyCN: 法庭同样在检验案件的事实，于是庭审与发动机测试共用了同一个词。

senses.title: A hard testing time
senses.definition: a person or situation that tests your patience or strength
senses.definitionCN: 考验人耐心或承受力的人或处境
senses.example: Looking after three children alone was a real trial.
senses.exampleCN: 独自照料三个孩子真是一场考验。
senses.why: Anything that puts you under pressure is testing you, so hard days wear the same label.
senses.whyCN: 任何给你压力的事都在检验你，于是艰难的日子也挂上同一种标签。

senses.title: The person who is tested
senses.definition: a person taking part in a test to be chosen for a team or a job
senses.definitionCN: 参加测试以争取进入队伍或获得职位的人
senses.example: Three new players were on trial with the club in July.
senses.exampleCN: 七月有三名新球员在俱乐部试训。
senses.why: The noun can name a thing tested or a person tested, because both stand in front of a judge.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既能指被检验的物，也能指被检验的人，因为两者都站在评判者面前。

intro.en: Trial is a noun made in English from the French verb trier, to sift or pick out, and it names whatever has been tested.
intro.cn: trial 是英语用来自法语动词 trier（筛、挑）造出的名词，指被检验过的东西。

items.en: Trier meant to sift grain or to sort things by quality.
items.cn: trier 意为筛谷物或按品质分类。

items.en: Tribulare and tritare lie behind French trier, all about rubbing or sorting.
items.cn: 法语 trier 的背后是 tribulare 与 tritare，都涉及摩擦或分选。

items.en: English formed trial on the French stem, first for the testing of metal and goods.
items.cn: 英语在法语词干上造出 trial，最初指检验金属与货物。

items.en: Law courts adopted the word for the hearing that tests a case.
items.cn: 法院借这个词指检验案情的庭审。

items.en: Everyday speech extended it to anything that tests a person.
items.cn: 日常语言把它扩展到任何考验人的事情。

note.en: The first group shows the try family, the second holds other words for tests and hearings.
note.cn: 第一组是 try 词族，第二组是其他表示测试与审理的词。

entries.definition: To make an attempt or test something.
entries.definitionCN: 尝试；试试

entries.definition: Annoying and hard to bear.
entries.definitionCN: 令人难受的

entries.definition: A test to choose players or workers.
entries.definitionCN: 选拔；试用

entries.definition: A check of quality or ability.
entries.definitionCN: 测试；检验

entries.definition: A session in which a case is examined.
entries.definitionCN: 听证；审理

entries.definition: A controlled attempt to find out something.
entries.definitionCN: 实验

normalIntro.en: Trial is try with a thin -al added: what you get when you try something over and over.
normalIntro.cn: trial 就是 try 加一个轻薄的 -al：反复尝试之后得到的那件事。

normal.en: The y of try becomes i before the suffix: trial.
normal.cn: try 的 y 在词尾前变成 i：trial。

normal.en: Stand trial means you are being tested in court.
normal.cn: stand trial 意为在法庭上受检验。

normal.en: A trial period is time given to see if something works.
normal.cn: trial period 是检验一段时间看是否可行的期限。

normal.en: The plural only adds s: trials.
normal.cn: 复数只加 s：trials。

normal.en: A clinical trial tests a medicine on people.
normal.cn: clinical trial 是在人身上检验药物。

abstract.en: A marker line painted on a test track.
abstract.cn: 试验跑道上画的一条标线。

abstract.en: A small sample of cloth pulled between finger and thumb.
abstract.cn: 指尖搓过的一小块布样。

abstract.en: A long day that keeps asking how much you can carry.
abstract.cn: 漫长的一天，不断问你能承住多少。

examples.en: The drug is being tested in a large clinical trial.
examples.cn: 这种药正在一项大型临床试验中检验。

examples.en: She is standing trial for the theft of two paintings.
examples.cn: 她因盗窃两幅画而受审。

examples.en: The first month is a trial period without any cost.
examples.cn: 第一个月是免付费试用期。

dict_mnemonic.text: trial 里有 try——凡 trial 就是 try 出来的东西。

root: 由法语动词 trier（筛、挑）的词干加 -al 构成，源自中世纪拉丁语 tribulare、tritare，本义与筛选、摩擦有关；同族词有 try、trying、tryout。

sensesIntro.en: First the test of an object, then the test of a case in court, then any hard test of a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是检验物件，再是法庭上检验案情，最后是任何对人的艰难考验。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a marked track and a ticking screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：画着标线的跑道与跳动的屏幕。

branches.en: The product branch: a thing tested before sale.
branches.cn: 产品分支：上市前被检验的东西。

branches.en: The court branch: a case tested by a judge.
branches.cn: 法庭分支：由法官检验的案件。

branches.en: The person branch: a day that tests you.
branches.cn: 人分支：考验你的一天。

branches.en: The testing branch: both asks whether it holds.
branches.cn: 检验分支：两者都在问它是否站得住。

branches.en: The strain branch: weighing a person or a fact.
branches.cn: 承重分支：称量一个人或一项事实。

intro.en: Trial is formed from the French verb stem tri plus the noun suffix -al, a pattern English still uses freely.
intro.cn: trial 由法语动词词干 tri 加名词后缀 -al 构成，这一构词法英语至今仍常用。

latinIntro.en: Latin tritare, to rub or grind, is behind the French stem, and the words below show the same origin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tritare（磨、擦）是法语词干的前身，下面的词显示同一来源。

items.example: The stem carries the act of sorting for quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载按品质分选的行动。

items.example: It turns trying into a trial.
items.exampleCN: 它把尝试变成一次试验。

items.example: The verb names the bare action.
The participle became an adjective of strain.
items.exampleCN: 分词变成了表示煎熬的形容词。

items.example: The noun names what was tried.
items.exampleCN: 名词指被试验的那件事。

items.example: Several trials produced the same answer.
items.exampleCN: 几次试验得出同样的答案。

items.meaning: a public test for a place
items.example: Out marks a full attempt to the end.
items.exampleCN: out 标记把事情试到底。

items.example: Re adds another attempt after a failure.
items.exampleCN: re 表示失败后再来一次。

definition_en: a sound, light, or action that carries a message, or a sign of something

definition_zh: 养老金；退休金；津贴；发给…养老金
definition_en: a regular sum paid to someone who has stopped working, a similar allowance for other reasons, or to give such a payment to someone
core_image: 一只按月寄到的信封，装着固定的生活费
scene: 厂里的老会计到了退休年纪，人事把一份表格推到他面前。 After forty years, he was pensioned off with a modest monthly income.
sceneCN: 这里是「发给…养老金、使退休」（第 3 个义项：动词用法）；句意为干了四十年后，他领着一笔不多的月钱被安排退休。

derivatives.zh: 由 pension 加表示「人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「领养老金的人」
加后缀 -able 构成，义为「有资格领取养老金的」
加后缀 -ary 构成，义为「养老金的；领取养老金的」

senses.title: Regular income after retirement
senses.definition: a sum of money paid regularly to a person who has retired from work
senses.definitionCN: 定期支付给已退休人员的钱
senses.example: She lives on a small state pension.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠一笔不多的国家养老金生活。
senses.why: Latin pensio began as a payment weighed out on a fixed measure, and that fixed measure is what makes the modern payment regular rather than earned hour by hour.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pensio 最初指按固定份量称出来的付款，正是这种「固定份量」让今天的这笔钱按月发放，而不是按小时挣来。

senses.title: A similar allowance for other reasons
senses.definition: a regular payment made for injury, widowhood or long service rather than for retirement
senses.definitionCN: 因伤残、丧偶或长期服务而定期领取的钱，而不是因为退休
senses.example: The widow receives a pension from the state.
senses.exampleCN: 这位遗孀从国家领取抚恤金。
senses.why: Once the word meant a periodic payment rather than a wage, it could cover any fixed allowance, because the timing, not the reason, defines it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指的不是工资而是定期付款，它就能覆盖任何固定补助，因为定义它的是发放的节奏，而不是发放的理由。

senses.title: To give someone a pension and end their work
senses.definition: to pay a pension to someone, usually when their working life is being brought to an end
senses.definitionCN: 向某人支付养老金，通常是在结束其职业生涯的时候
senses.example: The firm pensioned off three senior managers last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年公司让三位高级经理领养老金退休了。
senses.why: The verb turns the payment into an act done to a person; the particle off adds the sense of being set aside from the active staff.
senses.whyCN: 动词把「付款」变成对某人做的动作；小品词 off 又添上「被从在职人员中挪开」的意思。

intro.en: Pension goes back to a Latin verb for hanging and weighing, whose noun came to mean a payment measured out at a fixed time.
intro.cn: pension 可上溯到拉丁语中表示悬挂与称重的动词，其名词后来指在固定时间量出来的付款。

items.en: Pendere meant to hang and also to weigh and pay out, because goods were weighed against metal on a balance.
items.cn: pendere 意为悬挂，也表示称重和付款，因为货物要在天平上与金属对量。

items.en: Pensio named a weighing and then a payment, the sum measured out at an agreed time.
items.cn: pensio 先指称量，后指付款，即在约定时间称量出来的那笔钱。

items.en: Old French took pension as a payment or rent and passed it into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语把 pension 用作付款或租金，并在诺曼时期之后传入英语。

items.en: Middle English pension meant a fixed regular payment, often for service or favour.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pension 指固定定期付款，常因服务或恩惠而给。

items.en: Modern English narrowed the main sense to retirement income and grew a verb meaning to retire someone on such pay.
items.cn: 现代英语把主要义项收窄为退休收入，并长出「发养老金使某人退休」的动词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the derived forms and other words on the Latin stem for hanging and weighing; the near-meaning group collects kinds of regular payment.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词以及同一拉丁词干（悬挂、称重）上的其他词；近义组收各类定期付款。

normalIntro.en: The word hangs on a Latin verb for weighing and paying, and its family keeps the picture of a sum measured out at fixed times.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词挂在拉丁语表示称重与付款的动词上，同族词保留着「按固定时间量出一笔钱」的画面。

normal.en: Pendere means to weigh, so a pension is money that was once weighed out on a balance.
normal.cn: pendere 意为称重，所以养老金最初是天平上称出来的钱。

normal.en: Suspend and pendant share the same root: to hang, which is what a balance does before it settles.
normal.cn: suspend 与 pendant 同根，都是「悬挂」，这正是天平在稳定前的动作。

normal.en: Add -er and a pensioner is the person on the receiving end of the payment.
normal.cn: 加 -er，pensioner 就是收这笔钱的人。

normal.en: Pension off means to move someone onto a pension and out of the active list.
normal.cn: pension off 意为把某人转到养老金上、移出在职名单。

normal.en: Pension is the income; allowance is the wider word for any regular payment.
normal.cn: pension 是这笔收入本身；allowance 是更宽的词，指任何定期付款。

abstract.en: A pension is time turned into money: years of work are weighed and paid back month by month.
abstract.cn: 养老金是把时间换成了钱：多年的工作被称量，再按月还回来。

abstract.en: The word remembers a balance because retirement is an accounting of a whole working life.
abstract.cn: 这个词记着一架天平，因为退休是对一整段职业生涯的结算。

abstract.en: To be pensioned off is to be valued and set aside at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 被安排领养老金退休，是在同一刻既被计价、又被挪到一边。

examples.en: She lives on a small state pension.

examples.en: The firm pensioned off three senior managers last year.
examples.cn: 去年公司让三位高级经理领养老金退休了。

examples.en: His pension is paid directly into the bank.
examples.cn: 他的养老金直接打进银行账户。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「盼薪」——退休以后每个月盼着那笔薪水到账；记住 pension 是养老金。

root: 拉丁语 pendere（悬挂、称重、付款）派生名词 pensio（称量、付款），经古法语 pension 进入英语；同族词多与「悬挂、称量」有关。

sensesIntro.en: One core payment, measured out at fixed times, divides into retirement income, other allowances, and the act of putting someone on it.
sensesIntro.cn: 一笔按固定时间量出来的钱，分成退休收入、其他补助，以及「让某人领这笔钱」的动作。

latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族挂在 pendere（悬挂、称重）与名词 pensio（量出来的付款）上；英语经法语借入的是名词。
